error.album.invalid_id.message: This album could not be registered because its identifier is malformed.
error.album.invalid_id.context: HTTP 400 on POST /v1/albums (album provisioning, S-C25): album_id is not a canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID. Always a client bug — the id is derived deterministically from the account master key.

error.album.not_available.message: This album isn't available on your account.
error.album.not_available.context: HTTP 403 on POST /v1/albums (album provisioning, S-C25): the submitted album id cannot be bound to the caller. Deliberately identical whatever the reason, so the endpoint never reveals whether another account already holds that id.

error.auth.user_already_exists.message: An account with these details already exists.
error.auth.user_already_exists.context: High-level error for HTTP 409 on registration. Server sends code `error.auth.user_already_exists`; clients localize this message.

error.auth.invalid_credentials.context: High-level error for HTTP 401 on login. Server sends code `error.auth.invalid_credentials`.

error.auth.rate_limited.message: Too many attempts. Please wait and try again.
error.auth.rate_limited.context: High-level error for HTTP 429. Server sends code `error.auth.rate_limited`.

error.auth.revoke_proof_required.message: Confirm with your account key to log out of all devices.
error.auth.revoke_proof_required.context: HTTP 401 on POST /logout/all (slice S-C23): no readable master-key proof was presented. The global revoke is authenticated by an identity-key signature over a server-issued challenge, never by a session token, so a request without one revokes nothing at all — there is no partial success and nothing for the client to clear locally.

error.auth.revoke_proof_invalid.message: That didn't confirm as you. Nothing was logged out.
error.auth.revoke_proof_invalid.context: HTTP 401 on POST /logout/all (slice S-C23): a proof was presented but did not verify — an unknown, spent, or expired challenge; an account with no published device directory to anchor the identity key; a key that does not sign that directory; or a bad signature. Every reason is surfaced identically so the endpoint is not an oracle, and no session is revoked.

error.protocol.version_unsupported.message: This version of Capsule is no longer supported. Please update the app.
error.protocol.version_unsupported.context: HTTP 426 from the universal protocol handshake (invariant 1): the client's X-Capsule-Protocol date falls outside the server's accepted window.

error.quota.exceeded.context: HTTP 403 at upload-session creation when the declared size would cross the uploader's hard quota limit.

error.quota.grace_locked.message: Your storage has been full past the grace period, so edits are paused until you free space.
error.quota.grace_locked.context: HTTP 403 in the Grace-expired quota state: quota_used has stayed at/above the hard limit past the grace window, so metadata-growth writes (caption/tag edits, new share or upload links) are refused. Reads, deletes, and restore-from-trash still work; freeing space lifts it.

error.quota.peer_budget_exceeded.message: This source has reached its caching limit on your account.
error.quota.peer_budget_exceeded.context: HTTP 403 when a federated blob cached on a user's behalf would cross the per-(receiving_user, source_peer) caching budget (default 25% of the receiver's hard quota per source peer). Bounds how much one user can pull from any single peer.

error.blob.pending_upload.message: The original photo hasn't been uploaded from its device yet.
error.blob.pending_upload.context: Transient state, not a durability loss: an asset visible in the sync feed whose original blob has not been uploaded yet (staged uploads / awaiting-original). Distinct from 410 Gone.

error.directory.version_conflict.message: This device list is out of date. Capsule will refresh it before continuing.
error.directory.version_conflict.context: HTTP 409 on device-directory publish (threat-model invariant 23): the submitted DeviceDirectory's directory_version does not strictly advance the version already stored for the user. A non-advancing or regressing publish is refused so the server cannot roll back a revocation.

error.directory.malformed.message: The device list could not be read.
error.directory.malformed.context: HTTP 400 on device-directory publish: the request body is not a decodable signed DeviceDirectory document (bad CBOR, or a directory_version outside the representable range).

error.escrow.malformed.message: The recovery backup could not be saved.
error.escrow.malformed.context: HTTP 400 on master-key escrow store (slice S-C12): the request body failed the coarse size sanity bound (empty, or larger than any legitimate wrapped master key). The server keeps the blob opaque and never inspects the wrap format; the recovery-secret entropy floor is enforced client-side in core, not here.

error.enrollment.local_auth_required.message: Confirm it's you on this device to add another device.
error.enrollment.local_auth_required.context: HTTP 403 on POST /devices/enroll (slice S-C7): the access token is not fresh enough to stand in for the doc's fresh local device authorization. A valid session token alone cannot start a cross-device add — the caller must re-authenticate locally so a stolen, stale token cannot enroll a rogue device.

error.enrollment.rate_limited.message: Too many device-add attempts. Please wait and try again.
error.enrollment.rate_limited.context: HTTP 429 on POST /devices/enroll (slice S-C7): the caller exceeded the per-user enrollment-code issuance budget for the current window.

error.enrollment.code_refused.message: That device code didn't work. Generate a new one and try again.
error.enrollment.code_refused.context: HTTP 404 on POST /devices/enroll/redeem (slice S-C7): the submitted enrollment code is unknown, already redeemed, expired, or rate-limited. Every reason is surfaced identically (indistinguishable by design) so redemption is not an oracle.

error.enrollment.channel_not_found.message: This device-add session has ended. Start again.
error.enrollment.channel_not_found.context: HTTP 404 on the enrollment relay channel (slice S-C7): the channel handle is unknown or expired, so the server has nothing to relay between the two devices.

error.enrollment.relay_malformed.message: The device-add request could not be read.
error.enrollment.relay_malformed.context: HTTP 400 on the enrollment relay channel (slice S-C7): the request named an unknown direction or carried a missing/oversized opaque payload. The server never inspects the payload contents; this is a structural rejection only.

error.moderation.account_suspended.message: Your account is suspended. You can't upload or share until it's reinstated.
error.moderation.account_suspended.context: HTTP 403 at POST /upload session creation (slice S-C8): the account carries an admin/billing suspension flag. Distinct from quota and permission rejections so the client surfaces the right remediation. Suspension is an access-level action — the user's data is untouched and the block is reversible.

error.moderation.server_blocked.message: This server is blocked from federating with us.
error.moderation.server_blocked.context: HTTP 403 (federation pull / report intake, slice S-C8): the requesting peer server is on this server's blocklist, so its federated request — a pull or a moderation report — is refused at the federation-capability layer.

error.moderation.report_unsigned.message: The moderation report could not be verified.
error.moderation.report_unsigned.context: Federated report intake (slice S-C8, threat-model invariant 24): the report's Ed25519 signature did not verify against a known peer key — unsigned, tampered, or from an unregistered peer — or the report was structurally malformed. It is dropped before the admin queue, never surfaced.

error.moderation.report_rate_limited.message: Too many reports from this source. Please wait and try again.
error.moderation.report_rate_limited.context: HTTP 429 on federated report intake (slice S-C8, threat-model invariant 24): the per-(reporting_server, reported_user) report budget for the current window is exhausted. Backpressure defeats the false-flag / mass-report abuse vector rather than amplifying it.

error.federation.capability_invalid.message: This shared album's access could not be verified.
error.federation.capability_invalid.context: HTTP 401 on a federation pull (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 19): the presented capability token failed structural verification — a missing claim, a bad Ed25519 signature, an unparseable RFC 3339 claim, a wrong issuer, a not-yet-valid (nbf) token, or an expiry window wider than the 24h ceiling. The token never establishes access; the peer must obtain a fresh, well-formed one.

error.federation.capability_expired.message: This shared album's access has expired.
error.federation.capability_expired.context: HTTP 401 on a federation pull (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 19): the capability token is past its exp. Tokens live at most 24h; the peer must refresh before continuing.

error.federation.capability_revoked.message: Access to this shared album has been revoked.
error.federation.capability_revoked.context: HTTP 403 on a federation pull (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 19): the capability's jti is on the issuer's revocation list, OR the verifier is relying on a cached revocation list it can no longer refresh past the 15-minute staleness bound and therefore cannot confirm the jti — the fail-closed rule. Revocation is never outlived by making the list unreachable.

error.federation.audience_mismatch.message: This access grant is for a different album.
error.federation.audience_mismatch.context: HTTP 403 on a federation pull (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 19): the capability's aud (an urn:capsule:album:UUID) does not match the album the peer is pulling. The aud is matched against the album, never against the verifying server (a deliberate RFC 7519 deviation).

error.federation.scope_insufficient.message: This access grant does not cover the requested content.
error.federation.scope_insufficient.context: HTTP 403 on a federation blob fetch (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 19): a read-derivative-only capability tried to fetch a blob whose server-visible role is 'original'. Scope is enforced structurally against each blob's role.

error.federation.rate_budget_exceeded.message: This source has reached its request limit. Please wait and try again.
error.federation.rate_budget_exceeded.context: HTTP 429 on a federation pull (slice S-E2, threat-model invariant 21): the peer exceeded one of its per-peer transfer budgets — events/hour, bytes/hour, or CPU/hour. Each peer is its own blast-radius boundary; a busy or hostile peer cannot starve good ones.

error.federation.circuit_open.message: This source is temporarily backed off after repeated errors.
error.federation.circuit_open.context: HTTP 429 on a federation pull (slice S-E2): the peer spent its per-peer error budget on malformed input, tripping a circuit breaker that backs it off exponentially (5 / 30 / 60 minutes). Requests are short-circuited until the back-off elapses, so a buggy peer cannot DoS the server.

error.storage.invalid_request.context: HTTP 400 from POST /storage/verify (slice S-C3): a declared blob hash is not 64-char lowercase hex, or an asset_id is empty. Structural rejection before any verdict is computed.

error.storage.deep_rate_limited.message: Too many deep storage checks. Please wait and try again.
error.storage.deep_rate_limited.context: HTTP 429 from POST /storage/verify with deep=true (slice S-C3): the caller exceeded its per-user deep re-hash budget for the current window. Deep scans are server-priced (rate-limited and coalesced) so they cannot be turned into an I/O-amplification attack.

error.share.rate_limited.message: Too many attempts. Please wait and try again.
error.share.rate_limited.context: HTTP 429 on the public share serve path (slice S-C4): the per-source-IP or per-{opaque-id} serve rate limit engaged. Both limiters are charged on every /s/{opaque-id} request (metadata, blob, wrapped-secret) to throttle link enumeration; a not-found/revoked/expired link is an indistinguishable bodyless 404, never a distinct code.

error.sync.cursor_invalid.message: The sync session is out of date. Capsule will resync from the start.
error.sync.cursor_invalid.context: gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT (threat-model invariant 22): the opaque sync cursor failed its server MAC — forged, mutated, or lifted from another context. The client discards it and resyncs from an empty cursor.

error.sync.unauthenticated.message: Please sign in again to continue syncing.
error.sync.unauthenticated.context: gRPC UNAUTHENTICATED on the sync feed: the request carried no valid access token in the `authorization` call metadata.

error.upload.malformed_request.context: HTTP 400 on POST /upload: unknown or missing JSON fields. The transport JSON is strict (deny unknown fields).

error.upload.unknown_crypto_suite.message: This app version uses an encryption suite the server doesn't recognize.
error.upload.unknown_crypto_suite.context: HTTP 400, invariant 2: crypto_suite_id not in the server's inventory.

error.upload.invalid_hash.message: The upload's declared content hash is invalid.
error.upload.invalid_hash.context: HTTP 400, invariant 3: hash is not lowercase hex or its length doesn't match the suite's digest length.

error.upload.invalid_size.message: The upload's declared size is invalid.
error.upload.invalid_size.context: HTTP 400, invariant 4: declared size is zero or negative.

error.upload.file_too_large.message: This file exceeds the server's size limit.
error.upload.file_too_large.context: HTTP 413, invariant 4: declared size (or cumulative bytes) exceeds max_file_size.

error.upload.unsupported_content_type.message: This file type is not supported.
error.upload.unsupported_content_type.context: HTTP 400, invariant 5: content_type outside the closed enum for the pinned protocol version.

error.upload.album_access_denied.message: You don't have permission to add photos to this album.
error.upload.album_access_denied.context: HTTP 403, invariant 6: album missing, no write capability, or album protocol version drift.

error.upload.device_not_authorized.message: This device isn't authorized to upload. Re-enroll it and try again.
error.upload.device_not_authorized.context: HTTP 403, invariant 7: manifest envelope's created_by_device is not in the uploader's device directory.

error.upload.timestamp_out_of_range.message: Your device's clock appears to be wrong. Check its date and time.
error.upload.timestamp_out_of_range.context: HTTP 400, invariant 8: envelope timestamp outside the gross-drift sanity window (default ±30 days).

error.upload.envelope_mismatch.message: The upload request contradicts its signed manifest.
error.upload.envelope_mismatch.context: HTTP 400: top-level request fields (crypto_suite_id, protocol_version, album_id) disagree with the manifest_envelope. Always a client bug.

error.upload.owner_not_permitted.message: You can't upload on behalf of this user.
error.upload.owner_not_permitted.context: HTTP 403: owner_id differs from the uploader without a verified relationship.

error.upload.duplicate_blob.context: HTTP 409 on POST /upload when the content hash is already finalized for this owner+album. Carries the existing asset reference; the client resolves it as a merge, not an error surface.

error.upload.unsupported_media_type.message: Upload data was sent in an unsupported format.
error.upload.unsupported_media_type.context: HTTP 415, invariant 10: PATCH body Content-Type is not application/octet-stream.

error.upload.empty_chunk.message: An upload chunk cannot be empty.
error.upload.empty_chunk.context: HTTP 400, invariant 10: zero-length PATCH body. Always a client bug; never accepted as a no-op.

error.upload.chunk_not_aligned.message: An upload chunk was incorrectly sized.
error.upload.chunk_not_aligned.context: HTTP 400, invariant 10: non-final chunk not a multiple of 4 KiB.

error.upload.chunk_too_large.message: An upload chunk exceeded the maximum chunk size.
error.upload.chunk_too_large.context: HTTP 413, invariant 10: chunk body larger than the 16 MiB protocol maximum.

error.upload.missing_offset.message: The upload request was missing its position marker.
error.upload.missing_offset.context: HTTP 400, invariant 9 family: X-Capsule-Offset header missing or unparseable on PATCH.

error.upload.missing_checksum.message: The upload request was missing its integrity checksum.
error.upload.missing_checksum.context: HTTP 400, invariant 12: X-Capsule-Checksum header missing or not valid lowercase-hex SHA-256. The checksum is required — the idempotency tuple is undefined without it.

error.upload.checksum_mismatch.message: Upload data was corrupted in transit. Retrying…
error.upload.checksum_mismatch.context: HTTP 400, invariant 12: SHA-256 of the received body doesn't match X-Capsule-Checksum. Nothing was persisted; the client re-sends the same chunk.

error.upload.offset_mismatch.message: The upload got out of sync and is realigning.
error.upload.offset_mismatch.context: HTTP 409, invariant 9: PATCH offset differs from the current received-byte count. Response carries the authoritative X-Capsule-Offset; the client realigns.

error.upload.chunk_conflict.message: The upload sent conflicting data and was stopped.
error.upload.chunk_conflict.context: HTTP 409, invariant 12: a PATCH at an already-acknowledged offset with a different chunk hash — the structural defense against a faulty client retrying with garbage.

error.upload.size_exceeded.message: The upload sent more data than it declared.
error.upload.size_exceeded.context: HTTP 400, invariant 11: cumulative received bytes would exceed the declared size. Session moves to FailedProcessing.

error.upload.session_not_found.message: The upload session expired. Starting over…
error.upload.session_not_found.context: HTTP 404: unknown, expired, or pressure-discarded session — deliberately indistinguishable. The client re-creates the session and re-uploads that blob.

error.upload.session_not_active.context: HTTP 409: PATCH/DELETE against a session that is finalizing or terminal. The outcome is read via HEAD.

error.upload.finalize_in_progress.message: This upload is already being finalized.
error.upload.finalize_in_progress.context: HTTP 409: a concurrent finalization attempt lost the atomic status compare-and-set.

error.upload.receipt_not_available.message: The upload hasn't finished, so its storage receipt isn't available yet.
error.upload.receipt_not_available.context: HTTP 409, invariant 33: GET /upload/{id}/receipt before the session reached Completed. The receipt is signed inside the finalization transaction; the client retries after Completed.

error.upload.content_hash_mismatch.message: The upload failed integrity verification and was discarded.
error.upload.content_hash_mismatch.context: HTTP 400 at finalization, invariant 14: recomputed ciphertext hash differs from the declared hash. Treated as corruption/tampering; blob and pending row are deleted.

error.upload.envelope_rejected.message: The upload's signed manifest failed validation.
error.upload.envelope_rejected.context: HTTP 400 at finalization, invariant 15: envelope re-validation (rerun of invariants 1–8) failed inside the finalization transaction.

error.upload.forbidden.message: You don't have access to this upload.
error.upload.forbidden.context: HTTP 403: caller is neither the session's uploader nor the asset owner.

error.upload.storage_inconsistent.message: The server hit a storage problem. Please try again.
error.upload.storage_inconsistent.context: HTTP 500: the upload file's on-disk length diverged from the session's expected offset. Server-side inconsistency, never the client's fault.

error.upload.invalid_action.message: This change uses an action the album doesn't allow.
error.upload.invalid_action.context: HTTP 400 on POST /albums/{album_id}/ops, invariant 16: the manifest's action is outside the closed lifecycle-action set, or is create/replace (which ride the upload protocol, not this surface). Always a client bug.

error.upload.stale_revival.message: This change is based on an out-of-date version of the item.
error.upload.stale_revival.context: HTTP 409 on POST /albums/{album_id}/ops, invariant 17: the manifest's prior_provenance_hash does not match the asset's current provenance-chain head (a stale or forked position, e.g. a peer replaying an old manifest to revive a deleted asset).

error.upload.amk_regressed.message: This change references an older album key than the server has recorded.
error.upload.amk_regressed.context: HTTP 400 on POST /albums/{album_id}/ops, invariant 18: the manifest's amk_version regresses below the album's recorded epoch. The server counter is the monotonic backstop; MLS is the authoritative ceiling.

error.drop.cap_exceeded.context: HTTP 409 on POST /u/{opaque-id}/drop (web-upload, invariant 26): a cumulative per-link cap (total bytes or file count) is already exhausted for an otherwise-live link.

error.drop.malformed_descriptor.context: HTTP 400 on POST /u/{opaque-id}/drop (web-upload, invariant 30): the DropDescriptor is structurally malformed, its kem_ct length is wrong for the link's crypto suite, or the request carried an album/manifest/provenance field a drop must never carry.

error.drop.rate_limited.message: Too many attempts. Please wait and try again.
error.drop.rate_limited.context: HTTP 429 on POST /u/{opaque-id}/drop (web-upload, invariant 31): the per-{opaque-id} or per-source-IP drop-session rate limit engaged.

error.drop.passphrase_required.message: This upload link needs its passphrase.
error.drop.passphrase_required.context: HTTP 403 on POST /u/{opaque-id}/drop (web-upload): the link carries an Argon2id abuse-gate verifier and the guest supplied no proof, or a proof that did not verify.

error.drop.not_in_inbox.message: This drop is no longer available to adopt.
error.drop.not_in_inbox.context: HTTP 409 on POST /drops/{id}/adopt (web-upload, invariant 32): the manifest's ciphertext_hash does not reference a pending drop in the caller's own inbox.

device.cohort.label.previously_used.message: A device you've used before (last seen {last_seen})
device.cohort.label.previously_used.context: Devices screen: label for a device grouping (cohort) the account has enrolled before — e.g. after reinstalling the app. Assert-don't-litigate copy: it states recognition, it never asks the user to confirm or deny. {last_seen} is a formatted date the app supplies.

device.cohort.label.this_device.context: Devices screen: label for the device grouping that contains the session currently signed in.

device.cohort.label.new_device.context: Devices screen: label for a device grouping (cohort) seen for the first time on this account.

device.cohort.support.report.message: Report a problem with this device grouping
device.cohort.support.report.context: Devices screen: the one-tap support action. Because a device grouping is an advisory hash the user cannot adjudicate, there is deliberately no 'this isn't my device' toggle; the dispute path is a support report carrying the cohort hash and session map.

share.viewer.opening.context: Guest share viewer (/s/…): loading state shown while the link is fetched and its scope is unwrapped client-side.

share.viewer.readonly_badge.context: Guest share viewer: badge marking the view as read-only — a share link never grants write access.

share.scope.album.context: Guest share viewer: heading when the link points at a whole album.

share.scope.asset.context: Guest share viewer: heading when the link points at a single asset.

share.items.context: Guest share viewer: count of assets the shared link covers.

share.expires.context: Guest share viewer: shown when the link has an expiry. {date} is a formatted date/time the app supplies.

ios.onboarding.step.photo_access.context: First-run step: grant access to the system photo library.

ios.onboarding.step.backup_scope.context: First-run step: choose which representations sync.

ios.menu.export.context: Menu item that exports the selected photos, applying the privacy strip.

ios.menu.select_all.context: Menu item that selects every item in the current view.

ios.menu.toggle_sidebar.context: Menu item that shows or hides the sidebar.

ios.menu.next_asset.context: Menu item that advances the viewer to the next photo.

ios.menu.previous_asset.context: Menu item that moves the viewer to the previous photo.

ios.menu.close_window.context: Menu item that closes the frontmost window.

ios.menu.zoom.years.context: Menu item that switches the timeline to one entry per year.

ios.menu.zoom.months.context: Menu item that switches the timeline to one entry per month.

ios.menu.zoom.days.context: Menu item that groups the timeline by day.

ios.menu.zoom.all.context: Menu item that shows every photo in one dense grid.

ios.scaffold.title.context: Heading on a placeholder screen that is reachable by navigation but has no implementation yet.

ios.scaffold.body.message: This screen is wired into navigation but has no interface yet.
ios.scaffold.body.context: Body text on a placeholder screen, explaining that the destination exists and routes correctly but is unimplemented.

ios.destination.missing.body.message: This is no longer in your library. It may have been removed, adopted, or resolved elsewhere.
ios.destination.missing.body.context: Shown when a route names an item — an album, a drop, a quarantined file — that no longer resolves.

ios.albums.default.name.context: Display name for the default container album, which is genuinely nameless in the data model. Every import that is not filed elsewhere lands here.

error.client.unclassified.context: Client-side fallback message used when a failure carries no specific catalog entry. Deliberately generic — the specific English diagnostic goes to logs, not to the screen.

error.client.unexpected.message: Capsule ran into an unexpected problem.
error.client.unexpected.context: Client-side code for an error the app never expected to see (something other than a typed Capsule error was thrown). Presented as a defect: offer a support report rather than a retry.

error.unexpected.message: Something went wrong during this transfer.
error.unexpected.context: Client-side code the transfer screens attach to an unrecognized thrown error, so the failure still reads as a transfer failure rather than as a blank state.

ios.asset.sync.awaiting_original.message: Original still on the device that took it
ios.asset.sync.awaiting_original.context: VoiceOver label for a photo you can see whose full-size file has not been uploaded from its own device yet. Informational, not a failure — never word it as an error.

ios.asset.sync.durable.context: VoiceOver label for a photo confirmed stored and retrievable on the home server. This is the safe state — no badge is drawn for it, but the label is read when one is.

ios.asset.sync.full_resolution_unavailab.context: VoiceOver label for a photo whose full-size version isn't available on this device, so a smaller one is shown. Informational, not a failure.

ios.asset.sync.newer_version.message: Written by a newer version of Capsule
ios.asset.sync.newer_version.context: VoiceOver label for a photo whose data a newer version of Capsule wrote. The data is intact and kept exactly as it is — never word this as damaged, corrupt, or unsupported.

ios.asset.sync.quarantined.context: VoiceOver label for a photo held pending a decision from you. Nothing has been deleted or changed; it is waiting for you to inspect, repair, or discard it.

ios.asset.sync.unreadable.message: Can't be opened on this device
ios.asset.sync.unreadable.context: VoiceOver label for a photo that is present but cannot be read here. It is badged rather than hidden, because a photo that simply vanished would be indistinguishable from lost data.

ios.asset.sync.uploading.context: VoiceOver label for a photo currently being uploaded.

ios.auth.common.defect.title.context: Heading of the sign-in error banner for a fault in the app itself, which the user cannot fix. Paired with a support report rather than a retry.

ios.auth.common.error.title.context: Heading of the sign-in error banner when a person has to fix something (a credential, a name already taken). The specific reason is shown underneath.

ios.auth.common.loading.context: Label beside the spinner on sign-in and setup screens. Present so the spinner is announced to VoiceOver rather than being silent.

ios.auth.common.offline.message.message: You can keep using Capsule on this device. This step will finish once the server is reachable again.
ios.auth.common.offline.message.context: Footnote under the unreachable-server banner. Reassurance, not an error — nothing has been lost.

ios.auth.common.offline.title.context: Heading of the sign-in error banner when the server is unreachable or the condition clears on its own.

ios.auth.common.retry.context: iOS button on a sign-in error banner that repeats the failed request. Shown only when retrying is honest for that failure.

ios.auth.common.upgrade.title.context: Heading of the sign-in error banner when this build and the server disagree about the protocol version. There is no negotiation — the app must be updated.

ios.auth.confirm.phrase.footer.message: Type the phrase exactly as shown. This action can't be undone.
ios.auth.confirm.phrase.footer.context: Footnote under the typed-phrase confirmation field, explaining why typing is required instead of a single tap.

ios.auth.confirm.phrase.mismatch.context: Status chip under the confirmation field while what has been typed does not yet match the required phrase. A work-in-progress note, not a rejection — keep it short.

ios.auth.confirm.phrase.required.context: Caption above the exact phrase a person must copy to confirm an irreversible action. The phrase itself is never translated.

ios.auth.login.credentials_rejected.context: Status chip after a rejected sign-in. Must never say which of the two was wrong — the server does not say either, and a more specific message would let someone test whether an account exists.

ios.auth.login.handle.label.context: Field label for the account handle, which has the form user@yourserver.tld.

ios.auth.login.handle.prompt.context: Placeholder in the handle field, showing the shape of a handle. Translate the 'you' part only if that reads more naturally; keep it a plausible example.

ios.auth.login.oidc.message: Sign In with Your Identity Provider
ios.auth.login.oidc.context: Button that hands sign-in to the identity provider the server uses for single sign-on.

ios.auth.login.passkey.context: Button that signs in with a passkey instead of a password. Shown only when the server supports passkeys.

ios.auth.login.password.label.context: Field label for the account password on the sign-in screen.

ios.auth.login.rate_limited.hint.message: Too many attempts — wait a moment before trying again
ios.auth.login.rate_limited.hint.context: Status chip shown after too many sign-in attempts.

ios.auth.login.submit.context: Primary button that submits the sign-in form.

ios.auth.login.submitting.context: Spinner label while the sign-in request is in flight.

ios.auth.login.subtitle.message: Sign in with the handle and password for your server.

ios.auth.login.totp.footer.message: Only if your account uses two-factor authentication. Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
ios.auth.login.totp.footer.context: Footnote under the verification-code field. The field is always shown, so the footnote says when it can be left empty.

ios.auth.login.totp.label.context: Field label for the one-time code from an authenticator app, on the sign-in screen.

ios.auth.path.footer.message: Either way, the credential only signs you in. The key that unlocks your photos is made on your device, and whoever checks your credential never sees it.
ios.auth.path.footer.context: Footnote under the sign-in-method cards. Important for someone signing in through an employer's identity provider: choosing single sign-on does not give that provider access to their photos.

ios.auth.path.local.action.context: Button on the server-password card that continues with that method.

ios.auth.path.local.description.message: Sign in with a handle and password held by this server.

ios.auth.path.local.title.context: Title of the card for signing in with credentials the server itself checks.

ios.auth.path.oidc.action.context: Button on the identity-provider card that continues with that method.

ios.auth.path.oidc.description.message: Sign in through the identity provider this server uses for single sign-on.

ios.auth.path.oidc.title.context: Title of the card for signing in through an external identity provider (OIDC single sign-on).

ios.auth.path.subtitle.message: Choose how you sign in to this server.

ios.auth.path.title.context: Heading of the screen that chooses between the server's own password ceremony and an external identity provider.

ios.auth.path.unsupported.description.message: This server didn't offer a sign-in method Capsule supports. Ask whoever runs it, or connect a different server.
ios.auth.path.unsupported.description.context: Empty-state description when the server offered no sign-in method this app understands.

ios.auth.path.unsupported.title.context: Empty-state title when the server offered no sign-in method this app understands.

ios.auth.server.change.context: Secondary button that clears the looked-up server and returns to the domain field.

ios.auth.server.discover.context: Primary button that fetches the server's published details for the entered domain.

ios.auth.server.discovering.context: Spinner label while the server's published details are being fetched.

ios.auth.server.domain.footer.message: Capsule looks up the server's details at this domain. Nothing is sent to it yet.

ios.auth.server.domain.label.context: Field label for the server's domain name.

ios.auth.server.domain.prompt.context: Placeholder in the server-domain field. An example domain — keep it as a domain, do not translate the words.

ios.auth.server.empty.description.message: Nothing at that domain answered as a Capsule server. Check the spelling and try again.
ios.auth.server.empty.description.context: Empty-state description when server lookup found nothing.

ios.auth.server.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when nothing at the entered domain answered as a Capsule server.

ios.auth.server.identity.api.context: Row label on the server identity card: the base address Capsule makes requests to.

ios.auth.server.identity.footer.message: Compare this signing key with the one the server's administrator published. Once you pin it, Capsule refuses to connect if the key ever changes.
ios.auth.server.identity.footer.context: Footnote on the server identity card explaining what checking and pinning the key are for.

ios.auth.server.identity.header.context: Heading of the card showing what the server published about itself.

ios.auth.server.identity.origin.context: Row label on the server identity card: the server's origin (scheme and host).

ios.auth.server.identity.signing_key.context: Row label on the server identity card for the server's public signing key, shown in groups of characters so a person can compare it by eye.

ios.auth.server.pin.context: Primary button that pins the server's signing key, so a later change of key is refused rather than trusted.

ios.auth.server.pinned.context: Status chip confirming this server's signing key is already pinned.

ios.auth.server.protocol.incompatible.message: This server speaks a protocol version this app doesn't. Update Capsule to connect.
ios.auth.server.protocol.incompatible.context: Warning under the protocol-version row when no version is shared with this build. Pinning is blocked while this shows.

ios.auth.server.protocol.supported.context: Row label on the server identity card for the range of protocol versions the server accepts. The value is a numeric range.

ios.auth.server.subtitle.message: Enter the domain of the Capsule server you want to use.

ios.auth.server.title.context: Heading of the screen where a server domain is entered and its identity checked.

ios.auth.signup.handle.label.context: Field label for the handle being claimed, which has the form user@yourserver.tld.

ios.auth.signup.handle.prompt.context: Placeholder in the handle field on the account-creation screen, showing the shape of a handle.

ios.auth.signup.handle.taken.message: That handle is already in use
ios.auth.signup.handle.taken.context: Status chip when the requested handle is taken. Keep short — it sits beside a warning symbol.

ios.auth.signup.password.confirm.context: Field label for retyping the new account password.

ios.auth.signup.password.label.context: Field label for the new account password.

ios.auth.signup.password.mismatch.context: Status chip while the two password fields differ.

ios.auth.signup.password.requirement.context: Footnote under the new-password field. The number is the client's minimum password length; keep the digits as they are.

ios.auth.signup.scope_note.message: This creates your account on the server and nothing more. The key that unlocks your photos is made on this device in the next step, and the server never sees it.
ios.auth.signup.scope_note.context: Footnote under the account-creation form, correcting the assumption that a server password protects the photos. It does not — the account password authenticates the session only.

ios.auth.signup.submit.context: Primary button that creates the account.

ios.auth.signup.submitting.context: Spinner label while the account is being created.

ios.auth.signup.subtitle.message: Choose a handle and password for this server.

ios.auth.welcome.later_note.message: You can connect a server later without losing anything you've already imported.
ios.auth.welcome.later_note.context: Footnote under the two first-run choices, making clear the device-only path is not a dead end.

ios.auth.welcome.local.action.context: Button that takes the device-only path from the first-run screen.

ios.auth.welcome.local.description.message: Import, organize, search, and export your photos entirely on this device. Nothing leaves it.
ios.auth.welcome.local.description.context: Description of the device-only first-run choice.

ios.auth.welcome.local.title.context: Title of the first-run card for using Capsule with no server at all. A full choice, not a way of skipping setup — keep it as substantial as the server card.

ios.auth.welcome.server.action.context: Button that takes the connect-a-server path from the first-run screen.

ios.auth.welcome.server.description.message: Back up your photos to a Capsule server you or someone you trust runs, and keep them in step across your devices.
ios.auth.welcome.server.description.context: Description of the connect-a-server first-run choice.

ios.auth.welcome.server.title.context: Title of the first-run card for connecting a Capsule server.

ios.auth.welcome.session_expired.message: This session has expired. Sign in again to reach your server.
ios.auth.welcome.session_expired.context: Footnote under an already-signed-in account whose session is no longer valid. Local photos are unaffected.

ios.auth.welcome.signed_in_as.context: Caption above the handle of an account already signed in on this device. The handle follows on the next line, so this does not end with a colon.

ios.auth.welcome.subtitle.message: Choose how you want to start.
ios.auth.welcome.subtitle.context: Subtitle on the first-run screen, above two equally weighted choices.

ios.auth.welcome.title.context: Heading of the first screen shown on a new install.

ios.crossdevice.aborted.description.message: The safety codes didn't match, so nothing was transferred and the code is dead. Start again with a new code.
ios.crossdevice.aborted.description.context: Description of the stopped-setup state. Say plainly that nothing moved; the user starts over rather than retrying into the same channel.

ios.crossdevice.aborted.restart.context: Button that issues a fresh code after a stopped setup.

ios.crossdevice.aborted.title.context: Heading shown after the safety codes were reported as different. The setup is over — this is not a retry prompt.

ios.crossdevice.cancel.context: Button that abandons the in-progress device setup and invalidates the code.

ios.crossdevice.code.description.message: On the other device, scan this code. If it can't scan, type the digits instead.
ios.crossdevice.code.description.context: Description of the step showing the enrollment code.

ios.crossdevice.code.expired.context: Status chip once the issued code is past its ten-minute life.

ios.crossdevice.code.fallback.context: Label above the digit form of the enrollment code, for a device that cannot scan. The digits are grouped in threes so they can be read aloud.

ios.crossdevice.code.fallback_note.message: Use these digits if the other device can't scan. They're safe to read aloud — the code works once, expires in ten minutes, and you'll still compare a safety code afterwards.
ios.crossdevice.code.fallback_note.context: Footnote under the typed form of the enrollment code, explaining why a shorter code is not a weakness.

ios.crossdevice.code.live.context: Status chip while the issued code can still be used.

ios.crossdevice.code.qr_note.message: Point the other device's camera at this code.

ios.crossdevice.code.title.context: Heading of the step showing the enrollment code in both forms.

ios.crossdevice.completed.description.message: The other device is set up and can now reach your library.
ios.crossdevice.completed.description.context: Description of the device-added success state.

ios.crossdevice.completed.device_id.context: Label for the identifier of the device that was just added.

ios.crossdevice.completed.title.context: Heading of the success state after a device has been enrolled.

ios.crossdevice.issue.context: Primary button that issues the one-time enrollment code.

ios.crossdevice.issue_again.context: Button that issues a fresh code after the previous one expired.

ios.crossdevice.issuing.context: Spinner label while the one-time enrollment code is being issued.

ios.crossdevice.local_auth_required.message: Unlock this device to add another one
ios.crossdevice.local_auth_required.context: Status chip when issuing a code was refused because it needs a fresh unlock on this device (Face ID, Touch ID, or the passcode), not merely a valid session.

ios.crossdevice.safety.acknowledge.message: The codes match and both devices are mine
ios.crossdevice.safety.acknowledge.context: Label of the switch confirming the safety check. It covers both halves deliberately — matching digits on a device you don't recognize is exactly the case this catches.

ios.crossdevice.safety.code.context: Label above the safety code itself, shown in the same groups on both devices so they can be compared character by character.

ios.crossdevice.safety.confirm.context: Primary button that accepts the safety comparison and continues setup. Enabled only once the switch above is on.

ios.crossdevice.safety.description.message: Both devices should show the same safety code. If anything were sitting between them, the codes would differ.
ios.crossdevice.safety.description.context: Description of the safety-code step. This comparison, not the enrollment code, is what stops someone relaying the setup.

ios.crossdevice.safety.fingerprint.context: Label for a device's short key fingerprint, shown beside its model so both can be checked at once.

ios.crossdevice.safety.loading.context: Spinner label while the safety code is being derived.

ios.crossdevice.safety.mismatch.context: Button that stops setup because the two safety codes differ. Styled as destructive, but it is the safe choice — do not soften it into a maybe.

ios.crossdevice.safety.mismatch_note.message: If the codes differ, stop. Nothing is transferred, and you can start again with a new code.

ios.crossdevice.safety.new_device.context: Heading of the card describing the device being added.

ios.crossdevice.safety.this_device.context: Heading of the card describing the device you are holding.

ios.crossdevice.safety.title.context: Heading of the step where the same code must appear on both devices.

ios.crossdevice.start.description.message: Capsule will show a code for the other device to scan or type. It works once and expires in ten minutes.

ios.crossdevice.start.title.context: Heading of the first step, where a one-time code is issued.

ios.crossdevice.subtitle.message: Set up Capsule on another device using this one.

ios.crossdevice.title.context: Heading of the screen that enrolls a second device from a device already signed in.

ios.crossdevice.transferring.context: Spinner label while the new device receives its keys.

ios.crossdevice.waiting.context: Spinner label while the issued code has not been used yet.

ios.custody.action.blocked.footer.message: Capsule won't release the copy on this device until your server confirms it holds this photo.
ios.custody.action.blocked.footer.context: Footer under the actions when releasing is not allowed. This gate is absolute — nothing local is freed on an unconfirmed verdict.

ios.custody.action.release.context: Destructive button that frees the copy on this device. Offered only once storage has been confirmed.

ios.custody.action.release.footer.message: Your server has confirmed this photo, so the copy on this device can be freed. Capsule downloads it again when you need it.
ios.custody.action.release.footer.context: Footer under the actions when releasing the local copy is allowed.

ios.custody.action.verify.context: Button that asks the server whether it still holds this photo. Cheap, and answers the common question.

ios.custody.action.verify_deep.context: Button that asks the server to re-read the stored bytes rather than trust its own records. Slower, and rate-limited by the server.

ios.custody.blob.indexed.context: Fact about one piece of a photo: your server has it recorded against this photo.

ios.custody.blob.retrievable.context: Fact about one piece of a photo: your server can actually hand it back.

ios.custody.blob.stored.context: Fact about one piece of a photo: your server has the bytes on disk. A checkmark or cross beside it carries the answer.

ios.custody.empty.description.message: Your server hasn't issued a receipt for this photo yet.
ios.custody.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the storage receipt screen. Not a failure — a receipt is issued once the upload finishes.

ios.custody.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the storage receipt screen.

ios.custody.field.absent.context: Shown in place of a value the receipt does not carry. Worth showing rather than leaving blank.

ios.custody.field.blob_role.context: Row label for which part of the photo this receipt covers, such as the original or a preview. The value is a short identifier shown as-is.

ios.custody.field.ciphertext_hash.context: Row label for the hash of the stored bytes, shortened for display. The full value belongs in a diagnostic export.

ios.custody.field.envelope_hash.context: Row label tying this receipt to the photo's own history. May be absent.

ios.custody.field.first_in_log.context: Shown in place of a previous receipt when this is the first one your server issued.

ios.custody.field.prior_receipt.context: Row label for the receipt this one links back to.

ios.custody.field.received_at.context: Row label for when the server took delivery. The value is a date and time.

ios.custody.field.sequence.context: Row label for this receipt's position in the server's log. The value is a number.

ios.custody.field.server.context: Row label for which server issued the receipt. The value is the server's identifier.

ios.custody.field.server_key.context: Row label for the key the server signed with, shown as a short fingerprint.

ios.custody.field.size.context: Row label for the stored size. The value is a formatted size.

ios.custody.link.context: Row that opens the storage receipt for this photo.

ios.custody.link.footer.message: Your server's signed statement that it holds this photo — what makes 'the server lost it' and 'it was never uploaded' tellable apart.
ios.custody.link.footer.context: Footer under the link to a photo's storage receipt.

ios.custody.log.chained.context: Shown when each receipt links to the one before it, so none can be removed unnoticed.

ios.custody.log.sequence.context: Row label for this photo's newest position in the server's receipt log. The value is a number.

ios.custody.log.title.context: Section header over the state of your server's receipt log for this photo.

ios.custody.log.unchained.context: Shown when the receipts don't yet link to one another. A fact, not a fault.

ios.custody.receipt.footer.message: The content hash here is what your server computed from the bytes it stored, not a number this device sent it. That's what lets a receipt settle a disagreement.
ios.custody.receipt.footer.context: Footer under one receipt's fields, explaining why the receipt counts as evidence.

ios.custody.release.confirm.action.context: Destructive confirm button in the release-local-copy dialog.

ios.custody.release.confirm.message.message: Your server has confirmed it holds this photo. Capsule will download it again whenever you need it.

ios.custody.release.confirm.title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that the on-device copy will be freed.

ios.custody.title.context: Navigation title of the screen showing your server's signed proof that it holds a photo.

ios.custody.verdict.durable.context: Storage verdict: your server holds this photo and can hand it back. This is the only state in which the copy on this device may be released.

ios.custody.verdict.durable.description.message: Your server holds this photo and can hand it back. The copy on this device can safely be released.

ios.custody.verdict.freshness.context: Footer under the storage verdict. %@ is a whole number of seconds, already formatted.

ios.custody.verdict.not_confirmed.context: Storage verdict: your server does not yet hold every part of this photo. Wording fixed by the design docs — do not soften it into 'confirmed' or harden it into 'lost'.

ios.custody.verdict.not_confirmed.descri.message: Your server doesn't hold every part of this photo yet. The copy on this device stays exactly where it is.
ios.custody.verdict.not_confirmed.descri.context: Explanation of the not-yet-confirmed verdict. Nothing local is released in this state.

ios.custody.verdict.receipt_missing.context: Storage verdict: the server holds the photo but has issued no signed receipt for it.

ios.custody.verdict.receipt_missing.desc.message: Your server hasn't issued a signed receipt for this photo, so there's nothing to check against.

ios.custody.verdict.stale.context: Storage verdict: the photo was confirmed stored, but the check is old enough to be worth repeating.

ios.custody.verdict.stale.description.message: This was confirmed a while ago. Check again to be sure it's still there.

ios.custody.verdict.unchecked.context: Storage verdict: Capsule hasn't asked the server about this photo yet.

ios.custody.verdict.unchecked.descriptio.message: Capsule hasn't asked your server about this photo yet.

ios.devices.cohort.assertion.context: Status chip on a device card whose entries were made by hardware seen previously. Stated as fact — there is deliberately no way to dispute it here, because nobody can check a hash by eye. Keep it a plain assertion, not a question.

ios.devices.cohort.explanation.message: Entries are grouped by device. Reinstalling Capsule enrolls new keys, so one phone can appear here more than once.
ios.devices.cohort.explanation.context: Footnote on a device card explaining why one physical device has several entries. Say it plainly; do not hedge or apologize for it.

ios.devices.cohort.ungrouped.context: Footnote on entries Capsule could not attribute to a known device — for example after a factory reset, which starts a new group by design.

ios.devices.device.current.context: Status chip marking the device you are using right now.

ios.devices.device.first_seen.context: Row label for the date a device first appeared on the account. The value is a date.

ios.devices.device.header.context: Section heading over the device entries within one device card.

ios.devices.device.last_seen.context: Row label for the date a device was last active. The value is a date.

ios.devices.device.revoke.context: Destructive button that revokes one device's keys. The device can no longer act on the account; what it already signed stays verifiable.

ios.devices.device.revoked.context: Status chip on a device whose keys have been revoked. Revoked entries stay listed on purpose, so the history stays auditable.

ios.devices.empty.description.message: Devices appear here once they're enrolled on your account.
ios.devices.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the devices screen.

ios.devices.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when the account has no enrolled devices.

ios.devices.loading.context: Spinner label while the device and session list loads.

ios.devices.platform.android.context: Platform name for a device running Android. A product name — do not translate.

ios.devices.platform.ios.context: Platform name for a device running iOS or iPadOS. A product name — keep Apple's own spelling.

ios.devices.platform.linux.context: Platform name for a device running Linux. A product name — do not translate.

ios.devices.platform.macos.context: Platform name for a device running macOS. A product name — keep Apple's own spelling.

ios.devices.platform.unknown.context: Platform name for a device that did not report a platform Capsule recognizes.

ios.devices.platform.windows.context: Platform name for a device running Windows. A product name — do not translate.

ios.devices.proof_required.message: Confirm with your account key to continue
ios.devices.proof_required.context: Status chip when the server asked for proof that you hold the account key and none was given. Signing every device out needs that proof; ending a single session does not.

ios.devices.revoke_all.context: Destructive button that ends every session on the account, including this one.

ios.devices.revoke_all.confirm.action.context: Destructive confirm button in the sign-out-everywhere dialog. Keep it short enough for a dialog button.

ios.devices.revoke_all.confirm.message.message: Every device, including this one, will be signed out. Your photos stay where they are.
ios.devices.revoke_all.confirm.message.context: Message in the sign-out-everywhere dialog. Reassures that this ends sessions only — nothing is deleted.

ios.devices.revoke_all.confirm.title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that every session will be ended.

ios.devices.revoke_all.proof_note.message: You'll be asked to confirm with your account key. Without it, nothing is signed out.
ios.devices.revoke_all.proof_note.context: Footnote under the sign-out-everywhere button, said in advance rather than discovered when the request fails. There is no partial success.

ios.devices.revoking.context: Spinner label while a revoke request is in flight.

ios.devices.session.created.context: Row label for when a session began. The value is a date.

ios.devices.session.current.context: Status chip for the session you are signed in with right now.

ios.devices.session.empty.context: Shown in place of the session list when a device has no recorded sessions.

ios.devices.session.expired.context: Status chip for a session that has passed its expiry.

ios.devices.session.expires.context: Row label for when a session stops working, whichever limit comes first. The value is a date.

ios.devices.session.last_used.context: Row label for when a session was last active. The value is a date.

ios.devices.session.live.context: Status chip for a session that is still valid.

ios.devices.session.revoke.context: Destructive button that ends one session. Any active session can do this.

ios.devices.session.revoked.context: Status chip for a session that was signed out deliberately.

ios.devices.subtitle.message: Every device enrolled on your account, and the sessions signed in on each one.

ios.devices.support_bundle.dismiss.context: Button that closes the gathered-report card.

ios.devices.support_bundle.first_seen.context: Label for the date this device grouping was first recorded. The value is a date.

ios.devices.support_bundle.hash.context: Label for the device-grouping identifier (the cohort hash), shown in groups of characters so it can be copied accurately.

ios.devices.support_bundle.ready.descrip.message: Include these details in your report. They identify the grouping only — no photos and no album contents.
ios.devices.support_bundle.ready.descrip.context: Description of the gathered device-grouping report.

ios.devices.support_bundle.ready.title.context: Heading of the card showing the gathered identifiers for a bug report.

ios.devices.title.context: Heading of the screen listing enrolled devices and the sign-ins on each.

ios.drops.caps.expiry.toggle.context: Switch that gives the upload link an expiry.

ios.drops.caps.file_count.toggle.context: Switch that caps how many files can be uploaded through the link.

ios.drops.caps.file_count.value.context: Stepper label for the file-count limit. The value beside it is a number.

ios.drops.caps.file_size.toggle.context: Switch that caps how large any one uploaded file may be.

ios.drops.caps.file_size.value.context: Stepper label for the per-file size limit. The value beside it is a formatted size.

ios.drops.caps.footer.message: Every limit is optional. Setting them keeps a link that gets out from costing you much.
ios.drops.caps.footer.context: Section footer under the upload-link limits.

ios.drops.caps.header.context: Section header over the limits placed on an upload link.

ios.drops.caps.issue.expiry_past.context: Warning about a combination of upload-link limits that can't be used.

ios.drops.caps.issue.file_over_total.message: The per-file limit is larger than the total, so it would never apply
ios.drops.caps.issue.file_over_total.context: Warning about a combination of upload-link limits that can't be used.

ios.drops.caps.issue.single_use_conflict.message: A single-use link accepts one file, so the file limit above won't apply
ios.drops.caps.issue.single_use_conflict.context: Warning about a combination of upload-link limits that can't be used.

ios.drops.caps.issue.zero.message: A limit of zero would stop anything being uploaded
ios.drops.caps.issue.zero.context: Warning about a combination of upload-link limits that can't be used.

ios.drops.caps.single_use.context: Switch that makes the upload link stop working after one upload.

ios.drops.caps.total_bytes.toggle.context: Switch that caps how much can be uploaded through the link in total.

ios.drops.caps.total_bytes.value.context: Stepper label for the total upload limit. The value beside it is a formatted size.

ios.drops.card.awaiting_review.context: Heading on one waiting upload's card. Normal and expected — nothing is wrong.

ios.drops.card.received.context: Row label for when a guest upload arrived. The value is a date and time.

ios.drops.card.via_link.context: Row label for which of your upload links a file arrived through. The value is a short link identifier.

ios.drops.claim.none.context: Shown when a guest upload arrived without a filename.

ios.drops.claim.unverified.context: Label before a filename a guest supplied. Capsule has no way to check it, so this warning comes before the name and never after it.

ios.drops.compose.create.context: Toolbar button that creates the upload link.

ios.drops.compose.default_album.context: Shown in place of an album name for the default container album, which has no name of its own. Match the name used elsewhere for that album.

ios.drops.compose.destination.context: Label of the picker choosing where accepted uploads are filed.

ios.drops.compose.destination.footer.message: Nothing goes into this album until you've reviewed it.
ios.drops.compose.destination.footer.context: Section footer under the upload-link destination picker.

ios.drops.compose.destination.header.context: Section header over the album guest uploads will be filed into once you accept them.

ios.drops.compose.issued.done.context: Button that clears the created upload link and returns the form to its starting state.

ios.drops.compose.issued.footer.message: Anyone with this link can send you files, within the limits you set. Revoke it from your links list when you're done with it.
ios.drops.compose.issued.footer.context: Footer under a newly created upload link.

ios.drops.compose.issued.header.context: Section header over a newly created upload link.

ios.drops.compose.issued.share.context: Button that hands the upload link to the system share sheet. It is also the accessible way to reach the link, since the address itself is hidden from VoiceOver.

ios.drops.compose.no_albums.description.message: Create an album first, so there's somewhere for uploads to go.
ios.drops.compose.no_albums.description.context: Empty-state description on the upload-link screen.

ios.drops.compose.no_albums.title.context: Empty-state title when there is no album for uploads to land in.

ios.drops.compose.passphrase.field.context: Field where the passphrase for the upload link is typed.

ios.drops.compose.passphrase.footer.message: This keeps strangers from filling your storage if the link gets out. It isn't what protects the files — they're sealed on the sender's device either way.
ios.drops.compose.passphrase.footer.context: Section footer under the upload-link passphrase. Named for what it is: a gate against abuse, not confidentiality. Do not call it encryption.

ios.drops.compose.passphrase.header.context: Section header over the optional passphrase for an upload link.

ios.drops.compose.passphrase.toggle.context: Switch that asks for a passphrase before anyone can upload through the link.

ios.drops.compose.scope.header.context: Section header over the plain statement of what an upload link can and can't do.

ios.drops.compose.scope.quota.message: Files waiting in your inbox count towards your storage.
ios.drops.compose.scope.quota.context: Statement about how waiting uploads affect your storage.

ios.drops.compose.scope.review_required.message: Everything sent waits in your inbox until you accept it.
ios.drops.compose.scope.review_required.context: Statement about what happens to files sent through an upload link.

ios.drops.compose.scope.write_only.message: Whoever has the link can send you files. They can't see anything in your library.
ios.drops.compose.scope.write_only.context: Statement of what an upload link allows.

ios.drops.compose.title.context: Navigation title of the screen that creates a link other people can send you files through.

ios.drops.detail.adopt.context: Button that accepts a guest upload into your library.

ios.drops.detail.claim.content_type.context: Row label for the file type a guest said their upload is. The value is shown as-is and is not verified.

ios.drops.detail.claim.size.context: Row label for a guest upload's size. The value is a formatted size.

ios.drops.detail.claims.footer.message: Whoever uploaded this chose these details. Capsule can't confirm any of them.
ios.drops.detail.claims.footer.context: Section footer under the sender-supplied details of a guest upload. The whole point is that these are claims, not facts.

ios.drops.detail.claims.header.context: Section header over details a guest supplied about their upload. None of them are verified.

ios.drops.detail.destination.context: Label of the picker choosing which album a guest upload joins.

ios.drops.detail.destination.footer.message: Accepting adds this to your library without uploading it again.
ios.drops.detail.destination.footer.context: Section footer under the destination picker. Accepting rewraps the file in place — the bytes never move.

ios.drops.detail.destination.header.context: Section header over the choice of album a guest upload will join.

ios.drops.detail.discard.context: Destructive button that rejects a guest upload.

ios.drops.detail.discard.confirm.context: Destructive confirm button in the discard-upload dialog.

ios.drops.detail.discard.confirm_message.message: The file is deleted for good and the space it used is freed. Whoever sent it isn't told.

ios.drops.detail.discard.confirm_title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that a guest upload will be deleted.

ios.drops.detail.none.description.message: Choose an upload to review it.
ios.drops.detail.none.description.context: Placeholder description in the detail pane of the guest-upload inbox.

ios.drops.detail.none.title.context: Placeholder title in the detail pane when no waiting upload is selected.

ios.drops.detail.outcome.adopted.context: Shown after a guest upload has been accepted.

ios.drops.detail.outcome.discarded.context: Shown after a guest upload has been discarded.

ios.drops.detail.preview.decoding.context: VoiceOver label for the spinner shown while a guest upload's preview is being decoded.

ios.drops.detail.preview.footer.message: Decoded on this device. Your server can't read this file.
ios.drops.detail.preview.footer.context: Section footer under the preview of a guest upload.

ios.drops.detail.preview.header.context: Section header over the preview of a guest upload.

ios.drops.detail.preview.unavailable.des.message: Capsule couldn't decode this file to show it. You can still accept or discard it.
ios.drops.detail.preview.unavailable.des.context: Description shown when a guest upload can't be previewed. Deciding without looking is a legitimate choice.

ios.drops.detail.preview.unavailable.tit.context: Title shown when a guest upload can't be previewed.

ios.drops.detail.received.context: Row label for when a guest upload arrived. The value is a date and time.

ios.drops.detail.title.context: Navigation title of the screen for accepting or discarding one guest upload.

ios.drops.inbox.empty.description.message: Files sent to you through an upload link will wait here until you accept them.
ios.drops.inbox.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the guest-upload inbox.

ios.drops.inbox.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the guest-upload inbox.

ios.drops.inbox.title.context: Navigation title of the list of guest uploads waiting for your review.

ios.enrollment.cancel.context: Button that abandons the setup ceremony. Leaving is deliberately an explicit act — the screen cannot be swiped away.

ios.enrollment.cancel.confirm.action.context: Destructive confirm button in the cancel-setup dialog.

ios.enrollment.cancel.confirm.message.message: Nothing is kept, and your account has no usable key until setup finishes. You'll start over from the beginning.
ios.enrollment.cancel.confirm.message.context: Message in the cancel-setup dialog, saying what abandoning halfway leaves behind.

ios.enrollment.cancel.confirm.title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that setup will be abandoned.

ios.enrollment.complete.action.context: Primary button that leaves the finished setup ceremony.

ios.enrollment.complete.description.message: Your keys are made and this device can reach your library.
ios.enrollment.complete.description.context: Description of the setup success state.

ios.enrollment.complete.title.context: Heading of the success state at the end of setup.

ios.enrollment.custody.footnote.message: Where this device keeps its keys. Said now rather than partway through, so nothing about it changes as setup runs.
ios.enrollment.custody.footnote.context: Footnote under the key-custody chip on the setup screen.

ios.enrollment.custody.secure_element.context: Status chip when this device has a secure element to hold its keys. Deliberately not 'hardware keys' — the post-quantum half is always sealed in software, so the claim is hardware-backed where the platform allows.

ios.enrollment.custody.software.message: Kept in software on this device
ios.enrollment.custody.software.context: Status chip when this device has no usable secure element and the keys live in software.

ios.enrollment.deferred.default_album.message: Your library album will be created before your first import.
ios.enrollment.deferred.default_album.context: Reason shown on the deferred step that creates the default album. Any device recreates it on demand, so nothing is lost.

ios.enrollment.deferred.description.message: Setup is complete on this device. The steps above will finish on their own once your server is reachable.
ios.enrollment.deferred.description.context: Description of deferred setup steps. They never block setup, and the copy must not suggest anything is wrong.

ios.enrollment.deferred.directory.message: This device works now. Your other devices will see it once the upload reaches your server.
ios.enrollment.deferred.directory.context: Reason shown on the deferred step that publishes this device's key list. The device is fully usable locally in the meantime.

ios.enrollment.deferred.header.context: Heading of the card listing steps that will complete once the server is reachable.

ios.enrollment.deviation.accepted.context: Status chip once the user has knowingly accepted software keys after the secure element refused.

ios.enrollment.failure.cancelled.context: Status chip after the user abandoned the setup ceremony.

ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.descript.message: Capsule couldn't put this device's keys in its secure storage. Trying again often works. You can also continue with keys kept in software.
ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.descript.context: Description of the secure-element failure. Retry is offered first because the refusal is often transient.

ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.deviatio.message: Software keys can be read by anything that gets into this device's storage, which hardware-backed keys resist. You can set this device up again later on hardware.
ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.deviatio.context: Footnote stating plainly what accepting software keys costs. The user must know before choosing — an unexplained fallback is a downgrade, not a choice.

ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.retry.context: Primary button that retries key generation in the secure element.

ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.software.context: Secondary button that accepts keys kept in software instead of in the secure element.

ios.enrollment.failure.hardware.title.context: Heading of the recovery card when the secure element would not generate keys. Rare, and sometimes temporary.

ios.enrollment.rail.header.context: Heading over the list of named setup steps.

ios.enrollment.running.context: Spinner label while the setup ceremony is running.

ios.enrollment.stage.default_album.expla.message: Creating the album your imports land in, so there's somewhere to put photos from the start.
ios.enrollment.stage.default_album.expla.context: One-sentence explanation of the library-album setup step.

ios.enrollment.stage.default_album.title.context: Name of the setup step that creates the album imports land in.

ios.enrollment.stage.device_keys.explana.message: Creating this device's keys, in its secure storage where the device has it.
ios.enrollment.stage.device_keys.explana.context: One-sentence explanation of the device-keys setup step.

ios.enrollment.stage.device_keys.title.context: Name of the setup step that creates this device's own keys.

ios.enrollment.stage.master_key.explanat.message: Creating the key that protects your library and storing it under your recovery phrase.
ios.enrollment.stage.master_key.explanat.context: One-sentence explanation of the account-key setup step.

ios.enrollment.stage.master_key.title.context: Name of the setup step that creates the key everything else in your library is protected with.

ios.enrollment.stage.publish_directory.e.message: Sending your signed device list to the server so your other devices recognize this one.
ios.enrollment.stage.publish_directory.e.context: One-sentence explanation of the publish-device step. This step may finish later without blocking setup.

ios.enrollment.stage.publish_directory.t.context: Name of the setup step that tells your other devices about this one.

ios.enrollment.stage.recovery_passphrase.message: Showing your recovery phrase and checking that you wrote it down.
ios.enrollment.stage.recovery_passphrase.context: One-sentence explanation of the recovery-phrase setup step.
Name of the setup step that shows the recovery phrase and asks for part of it back.

ios.enrollment.stage.user_identity_key.e.message: Creating the key that vouches for your devices to each other.
ios.enrollment.stage.user_identity_key.e.context: One-sentence explanation of the account-identity setup step.

ios.enrollment.stage.user_identity_key.t.context: Name of the setup step that creates the key proving your devices belong to you.

ios.enrollment.start.context: Primary button that begins the setup ceremony.

ios.enrollment.status.deferred.context: Status chip for a setup step that is done as far as the user is concerned and will complete in the background. Not a failure — it must not read as one.

ios.enrollment.status.done.context: Status chip for a setup step that finished.

ios.enrollment.status.failed.context: Status chip for a setup step that stopped.

ios.enrollment.status.pending.context: Status chip for a setup step that has not started.

ios.enrollment.status.running.context: Status label for the setup step currently in progress, shown beside a spinner.

ios.enrollment.subtitle.message: Capsule is making the keys that protect your library. Each step is listed below.
ios.enrollment.subtitle.context: Subtitle of the setup ceremony. There is no progress percentage on this screen by design — each step succeeds or fails on its own.

ios.enrollment.title.context: Heading of the first-device setup ceremony, which generates and publishes this device's keys.

ios.export.action.context: Toolbar button that starts the export.

ios.export.disposition.reduced.context: What happens to the location: it is coarsened rather than removed, so a photo still says roughly where it was taken.

ios.export.disposition.removed.context: What happens to one detail: it is taken out entirely.

ios.export.disposition.retained.context: What happens to one detail when the user has opted to keep identifying details in an export.

ios.export.field.camera_serial.context: Name of one detail removed when photos leave Capsule.

ios.export.field.contact_tags.context: Name of one detail removed when photos leave Capsule.

ios.export.field.device_id.context: Name of one detail removed when photos leave Capsule.

ios.export.field.location.context: Name of one detail removed when photos leave Capsule. Reduced to a city rather than removed outright.

ios.export.field.session_id.context: Name of one detail removed when photos leave Capsule.

ios.export.outcome.footer.message: Keeping identifying details has switched itself back off for the next export.
ios.export.outcome.footer.context: Footer after an export, saying out loud that the opt-in does not persist.

ios.export.outcome.partial.context: Shown when part of the export succeeded. The count of missing photos follows.

ios.export.outcome.prepared.context: Shown when every requested photo was exported.

ios.export.outcome.unavailable_count.context: Row label for how many photos couldn't be exported, usually because their full-size file isn't on this device yet. The value is a number.

ios.export.progress.context: VoiceOver label for the spinner shown while an export runs.

ios.export.retain.footer.message: Only for exports you're keeping yourself. Anything you then share carries these details with it.

ios.export.retain.toggle.context: Switch on the export sheet that keeps identifying details in the exported files.

ios.export.strip.footer.message: Exporting takes photos outside Capsule, so identifying details are removed by default.
ios.export.strip.footer.context: Section footer under the removed-details list on the export sheet.

ios.export.strip.header.context: Section header over the list of details removed from exported photos.

ios.export.summary.count.context: Row label for how many photos will be exported. The value is a number.

ios.export.summary.footer.message: Exported photos leave Capsule's protection. What you do with them afterwards is up to you.
ios.export.summary.footer.context: Section footer under the export summary.

ios.export.title.context: Navigation title of the sheet that exports photos out of Capsule.

ios.federation.album.partial.message: Some photos are out of reach
ios.federation.album.partial.context: Badge on a shared album where one contributor's server can't be reached. Nothing is lost — it is temporarily out of reach.

ios.federation.album.rendered_count.context: Row label for how many photos of a shared album are currently showing. The value is a number.

ios.federation.album.unreachable_owner.message: One server has been unreachable a long time
ios.federation.album.unreachable_owner.context: Badge on a shared album whose contributing server has been silent for weeks. Its photos are unreachable, not deleted.

ios.federation.album.untitled.context: Shown when nobody has given a shared album a name yet. A name that was never written is not an empty name.

ios.federation.compartment.cached.context: Row label for how much of another server's content is stored on your account. The value is a formatted size.

ios.federation.compartment.exhausted.message: Storage set aside for this server is full
ios.federation.compartment.exhausted.context: Badge when your account has reached the amount it will hold from one particular server. New content from it waits until room is freed.

ios.federation.constituent.count.context: Row label for how many photos one contributor has added. The value is a number.

ios.federation.detail.none.description.message: Choose an album to see where its photos come from.
ios.federation.detail.none.description.context: Placeholder description in the detail pane of the servers screen.

ios.federation.detail.none.title.context: Placeholder title in the detail pane when no shared album is selected.

ios.federation.detail.title.context: Navigation title of the detail screen for one album shared across servers.

ios.federation.empty.description.message: Albums shared across servers will appear here.
ios.federation.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the servers screen.

ios.federation.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the servers screen.

ios.federation.note.auto_recovery.message: Capsule keeps trying on its own. There's nothing you need to do.
ios.federation.note.auto_recovery.context: Statement about how unreachable servers are handled.

ios.federation.note.never_removed.message: Photos are never removed from your view because a server is quiet. They come back when it answers.
ios.federation.note.never_removed.context: Statement about what happens when a contributing server goes quiet.

ios.federation.note.no_kick.message: Nobody can remove someone else from this album. You can stop sharing your own photos; other people's are theirs to withdraw.
ios.federation.note.no_kick.context: Statement of an honest limit of shared albums. Do not paper over it.
