ios.federation.origin.available.context: Status of one contributor's server: answering normally.

ios.federation.origin.blocked.context: Status of one contributor's server that you've blocked.

ios.federation.origin.unavailable.context: Status of one contributor's server: temporarily unreachable. Their photos aren't lost.

ios.federation.origin.unreachable_owner.context: Status of one contributor's server after a long silence. Their photos aren't lost.

ios.federation.peer.backing_off.context: Status of another server: Capsule is spacing out its attempts after repeated failures.

ios.federation.peer.blocked.context: Status of another server that you've blocked.

ios.federation.peer.last_pull.context: Row label for when Capsule last got something from this server. The value is a relative time.

ios.federation.peer.reachable.context: Status of another server: answering normally.

ios.federation.peer.transient.context: Status of another server: a temporary outage.

ios.federation.peer.unknown.context: Status of another server Capsule hasn't tried to reach yet.

ios.federation.peer.unreachable.context: Status of another server after a long silence.

ios.federation.section.constituents.context: Section header over the people contributing to a shared album, each from their own server.

ios.federation.section.constituents_foot.message: Each person keeps their own photos on their own server. Capsule shows them together as one album.
ios.federation.section.constituents_foot.context: Section footer explaining how a shared album is assembled.

ios.federation.section.how.context: Section header over the plain statement of what a shared album can and can't do.

ios.federation.section.peers.context: Section header over the servers this album's photos come from.

ios.federation.state.unreachable_owner.message: A server hasn't answered in a long time. Its photos will come back if it does.
ios.federation.state.unreachable_owner.context: Notice on a shared album with a long-unreachable contributor. Non-destructive and temporary — never imply the data is gone.

ios.federation.summary.complete_footer.message: Every contributor's server is reachable, so you're seeing the whole album.
ios.federation.summary.complete_footer.context: Section footer on a shared album where everything is reachable.

ios.federation.summary.partial_footer.message: You're seeing everything Capsule can reach right now. The rest is on servers that aren't answering — nothing has been removed, and it returns when they do.
ios.federation.summary.partial_footer.context: Section footer on a shared album with unreachable contributors. The shortfall is reach, not loss — this distinction is the whole point of the sentence.

ios.federation.title.context: Navigation title of the screen listing shared albums whose contents come from more than one server.

ios.import.conflict.destructive.note.message: This replaces the copy already in your library
ios.import.conflict.destructive.note.context: Warning beside a conflict answer that overwrites an existing photo.

ios.import.conflict.kind.destination_dif.message: Already in your library, in a different album
ios.import.conflict.kind.destination_dif.context: Describes a conflict: the photo is here already but filed somewhere else.

ios.import.conflict.kind.duplicate_with_.message: Already in your library, with details this copy doesn't have
ios.import.conflict.kind.duplicate_with_.context: Describes a conflict: the photo is already here, but the incoming copy carries information the existing one lacks.

ios.import.conflict.kind.existing_is_edi.message: The copy in your library has been edited
ios.import.conflict.kind.existing_is_edi.context: Describes a conflict: the existing photo has edits the incoming copy does not.

ios.import.conflict.kind.same_name_diffe.context: Describes a conflict: a photo with this name is already here, but it isn't the same picture.

ios.import.conflict.kind.unknown.message: A conflict this version of Capsule doesn't recognize
ios.import.conflict.kind.unknown.context: Describes a conflict written by a newer version. The data is intact — do not word this as damaged or invalid.

ios.import.conflict.resolution.keep_both.context: Conflict answer: import the new photo and keep the one already here.

ios.import.conflict.resolution.merge_int.context: Conflict answer: fold the incoming details into the photo already here.

ios.import.conflict.resolution.replace_e.context: Conflict answer: the incoming photo takes the place of the one already here. This is the destructive choice.

ios.import.conflict.resolution.skip_inco.context: Conflict answer: leave the library as it is and don't import this photo.

ios.import.conflict.resolution.unknown.context: Conflict answer written by a newer version of Capsule that this one doesn't understand. Shown so the choice is visible rather than silently changed.

ios.import.history.deferred.context: Row label for photos that imported fully but whose previews haven't been made yet. Counted separately from failures on purpose — nothing is missing except the preview.

ios.import.history.dismiss.context: Destructive button that removes one entry from the import history. The photos it imported are not affected.

ios.import.history.elapsed.context: Row label for how long a past import ran. The value is a formatted duration.

ios.import.history.empty.description.message: Imports you run will be listed here.
ios.import.history.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the import history screen.

ios.import.history.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when nothing has been imported yet.

ios.import.history.failed.context: Row label for how many photos failed in a past import and can be retried. The value is a formatted number.

ios.import.history.imported.context: Row label for how many photos a past import brought in. The value is a formatted number.

ios.import.history.mode.context: Row label for whether a past import copied or moved its source files.

ios.import.history.outcome.cancelled.context: Outcome of a past import the user stopped.

ios.import.history.outcome.completed.context: Outcome of a past import that finished with nothing failing.

ios.import.history.outcome.completed_wit.context: Outcome of a past import that finished, but some photos failed.

ios.import.history.outcome.running.context: Outcome of a past import that is still in progress.

ios.import.history.rerun.context: Button that plans a fresh import from the same source as a past one.

ios.import.history.skipped.context: Row label for how many photos a past import skipped. The value is a formatted number.

ios.import.history.title.context: Navigation title of the screen listing past imports.

ios.import.kind.app_collection.context: Name of the source kind that reads a collection another app manages.

ios.import.kind.camera_roll.context: Name of the source kind that reads the device's own photo library.

ios.import.kind.folder.context: Name of the source kind that reads a folder on disk.

ios.import.kind.removable_volume.context: Name of the source kind that reads a memory card or external drive.

ios.import.kind.screenshots.context: Name of the source kind that reads the device's screenshots.

ios.import.kind.takeout_archive.context: Name of the source kind that unpacks an export archive from another photo product.

ios.import.kind.unknown.context: Name shown for a source kind this version of Capsule doesn't recognize. Not an error — a newer version may have written it.

ios.import.kind.watched_dir.context: Name of the source kind that keeps watching a folder for new files after the first import.

ios.import.plan.confirm.context: Primary button that starts the import. %@ is the number of photos that will be imported, already formatted. The count is on the button deliberately — a bare 'Import' at the foot of a long list can't be checked before pressing.

ios.import.plan.confirm.blocked.message: Answer every conflict above and make room on this device to continue.
ios.import.plan.confirm.blocked.context: Note under a disabled import button, saying what is standing in the way.

ios.import.plan.conflict.resolution.head.context: Label of the picker that answers one conflict, and its VoiceOver label.

ios.import.plan.destination.footer.message: You can move photos to another album after importing.
ios.import.plan.destination.footer.context: Section footer under the import destination.

ios.import.plan.destination.header.context: Section header over the album these photos will land in.

ios.import.plan.destination.reason.context: The line under the destination album. %@ is one of the destination reason sentences and is already a complete sentence — do not fold it into a longer clause.

ios.import.plan.destination.title.context: Label before the destination album's name. The album name follows on the same line, so this does not end with a colon.

ios.import.plan.destination.unnamed.context: Shown in place of an album name for the default container album, which has no name of its own. Match the name used elsewhere for that album.

ios.import.plan.empty.description.message: Everything in this source is already in your library.
ios.import.plan.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the import plan screen.

ios.import.plan.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when the plan would import nothing.

ios.import.plan.list.add.header.context: Section header over the expanded list of photos that will be imported.

ios.import.plan.list.conflicts.header.context: Section header over the expanded list of conflicts. Each one must be answered before importing.

ios.import.plan.list.skip.header.context: Section header over the expanded list of photos that will not be imported. Every row states its reason.

ios.import.plan.mode.copy.context: Import mode: the source files are left where they are.

ios.import.plan.mode.header.context: Row label for whether the import copies or moves the source files. The value is the mode's name.

ios.import.plan.mode.move.context: Import mode: the source files are deleted once the photos are safely stored.

ios.import.plan.mode.unknown.context: Import mode written by a newer version of Capsule that this one doesn't recognize.

ios.import.plan.move.warning.message: Your source files will be deleted once each photo is safely stored on your server
ios.import.plan.move.warning.context: Warning shown when the import is set to move rather than copy. Deletion happens only after storage is confirmed.

ios.import.plan.reason.derived_default.message: It's your library album, used when no other rule applies.
ios.import.plan.reason.derived_default.context: Reason sentence: nothing else matched, so imports land in the default container album.

ios.import.plan.reason.explicit_pick.context: Reason sentence: the user picked the destination album themselves.

ios.import.plan.reason.owner_pointer.context: Reason sentence: the destination is the album your account points at by default.

ios.import.plan.reason.scope_override.message: A rule you set for this source sends photos here.
ios.import.plan.reason.scope_override.context: Reason sentence: a per-source rule chose the destination without the user doing anything this time.

ios.import.plan.reason.source_kind_defau.message: It's the default album for this kind of source.
ios.import.plan.reason.source_kind_defau.context: Reason sentence: the destination is the default for this kind of import source.

ios.import.plan.skip.reason.duplicate.context: Reason line under a photo that will be skipped because Capsule already has it.

ios.import.plan.skip.reason.unreadable.context: Reason line under a photo that will be skipped because it could not be read — usually a permissions problem.

ios.import.plan.skip.reason.unsupported.message: Capsule can't read this file type
ios.import.plan.skip.reason.unsupported.context: Reason line under a photo that will be skipped because its format is not supported.

ios.import.plan.space.available.context: Row label for how much space is free on the device. The value is a formatted size.

ios.import.plan.space.comfortable.context: Verdict when the device has plenty of space.

ios.import.plan.space.enable_streaming.context: Button that re-plans the import so it keeps less on this device as it runs.

ios.import.plan.space.footer.message: Measured against this import, not your whole library.
ios.import.plan.space.footer.context: Section footer under the free-space meter.

ios.import.plan.space.free_up.context: Button that opens the screen for reclaiming space on this device.

ios.import.plan.space.header.context: Section header over the free-space meter, and the VoiceOver label for the meter.

ios.import.plan.space.insufficient.message: Not enough room. Free up %2$@ to import these %1$@ photos.
ios.import.plan.space.insufficient.context: Verdict when the import does not fit. %1$@ is the photo count and %2$@ is the shortfall, both already formatted. Naming the exact shortfall is the point — keep both values.

ios.import.plan.space.required.context: Row label for how much space this import needs. The value is a formatted size.

ios.import.plan.space.streaming.message: This will fit, but barely. Streaming keeps less on this device as it goes.
ios.import.plan.space.streaming.context: Verdict when the import fits but leaves little room. Streaming is offered as the remedy instead of deleting anything.

ios.import.plan.streaming.enabled.message: Streaming is on, so Capsule keeps less on this device as the import runs.
ios.import.plan.streaming.enabled.context: Note shown when streaming is enabled for this import.

ios.import.plan.summary.caption.context: Caption under the import plan headline, and its VoiceOver label. The headline itself is the count and size.

ios.import.plan.summary.headline.context: Headline of the import plan: the item count, then the total size. Both values arrive already formatted for the locale. Translate the separator if a middle dot is wrong for your language; keep %1$@ and %2$@ in an order that reads naturally.

ios.import.plan.tile.add.context: Label under the count of photos that will be imported. Sits under a large number on a small tile — keep it to one or two words.

ios.import.plan.tile.conflicts.context: Label under the count of photos needing a decision. Sits under a large number on a small tile — keep it to one or two words.

ios.import.plan.tile.skip.context: Label under the count of photos that will not be imported. Sits under a large number on a small tile — keep it to one or two words.

ios.import.plan.title.context: Navigation title of the third import step, where the user sees what will happen before anything is written.

ios.import.run.cancel.context: Button that stops the run. Photos already imported stay imported.

ios.import.run.cancelled.description.message: You stopped the import. Photos that already finished are in your library; the rest were left alone.
ios.import.run.cancelled.description.context: Note under a stopped import run.

ios.import.run.cancelled.title.context: Status shown when the user stopped the run.

ios.import.run.done.title.context: Status shown when the run finished.

ios.import.run.empty.description.message: This import has nothing left to do.
ios.import.run.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the import run screen.

ios.import.run.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when the run has no photos to process.

ios.import.run.failures.context: Row label for how many photos failed and can be retried. The value is a formatted number.

ios.import.run.items.header.context: Section header over the per-photo rows of a running import.

ios.import.run.progress.context: Progress line under the import bar: photos finished, then photos in total. Both values arrive already formatted.

ios.import.run.retry.context: Button on one failed photo's row that tries it again.

ios.import.run.retry_all.context: Button that retries every photo that failed in this run.

ios.import.run.stage.done.context: Stage of one photo in a run: finished.

ios.import.run.stage.encrypting.context: Stage of one photo in a run: being cryptographically wrapped before it leaves the device. 'Sealing' is Capsule's term for this — keep it distinct from any word for locking or hiding.

ios.import.run.stage.failed.context: Stage of one photo in a run: stopped with an error. The reason is shown under it.

ios.import.run.stage.processing.context: Stage of one photo in a run: being read and prepared.

ios.import.run.stage.queued.context: Stage of one photo in a run: waiting its turn.

ios.import.run.stage.unknown.context: Stage written by a newer version of Capsule that this one doesn't recognize.

ios.import.run.stage.uploading.context: Stage of one photo in a run: being sent to the server.

ios.import.run.title.context: Navigation title of the fourth import step, the run itself, and the VoiceOver label for its progress bar.

ios.import.scan.bytes.context: Row label for the total size of what the scan has found. The value is a formatted size.

ios.import.scan.cancel.context: Button that stops the scan in progress. Nothing has been imported yet.

ios.import.scan.cancelled.description.message: You stopped the scan. Nothing was imported, and you can scan again whenever you like.

ios.import.scan.cancelled.title.context: Status shown when the user stopped the scan.

ios.import.scan.complete.context: Status shown when the scan finished.

ios.import.scan.continue.context: Primary button that takes the finished scan to the plan step.

ios.import.scan.current.context: Row label for the file the scan is reading right now. The value is a file name.

ios.import.scan.empty.description.message: There's nothing here Capsule can import.
ios.import.scan.empty.description.context: Empty-state description when a scan found nothing.

ios.import.scan.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when the scan found no photos.

ios.import.scan.found.context: Row label for how many items the scan has found. The value is a formatted number.

ios.import.scan.header.context: Section header over the scan progress, and the VoiceOver label for the progress indicator.

ios.import.scan.location.context: Row label for where the source is. The value is a folder or file name.

ios.import.scan.scanning.context: Label on the scan progress bar while it is running.

ios.import.scan.source.context: Row label for the kind of source being scanned. The value is the source kind's name.

ios.import.scan.title.context: Navigation title of the second import step, which reads the chosen source.

ios.import.scan.unreadable.context: Section header over files the scan could not open. They are listed rather than skipped silently.

ios.import.scan.unreadable.footer.message: These files couldn't be opened — usually a permissions problem. They won't be imported.
ios.import.scan.unreadable.footer.context: Section footer under the list of unreadable files.

ios.import.source.choose.context: Status on a source row that needs the user to point at a folder or a file first.

ios.import.source.empty.description.message: Capsule found nothing on this device to import from.
ios.import.source.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the import source picker.

ios.import.source.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when this device offers no import source.

ios.import.source.files.detail.message: Asks for a folder, then imports the photos in it once.
ios.import.source.files.detail.context: Detail line under the Files source row.

ios.import.source.files.title.context: Title of the source row that imports from a folder chosen in the system file picker.

ios.import.source.footer.message: Nothing is imported until you've seen what will happen.
ios.import.source.footer.context: Section footer under the list of import sources.

ios.import.source.header.context: Section header over the list of import sources.

ios.import.source.photos.detail.message: Reads the photos already on this device. Nothing is deleted from your library.
ios.import.source.photos.detail.context: Detail line under the photo-library source row, saying what tapping it will do.

ios.import.source.photos.title.context: Title of the source row that imports from the device's own photo library.

ios.import.source.ready.context: Status on a source row that can be scanned immediately, because Capsule already knows where it is.

ios.import.source.removable_volume.detai.message: Imports from a card or drive attached to this Mac.
ios.import.source.removable_volume.detai.context: Detail line under the removable-volume source row.

ios.import.source.removable_volume.title.context: Title of the source row that imports from a mounted card or external drive. Mac only.

ios.import.source.takeout.detail.message: Unpacks an export archive from another photo service and imports what's inside.
ios.import.source.takeout.detail.context: Detail line under the Takeout archive source row.

ios.import.source.takeout.title.context: Title of the source row that imports from an export archive made by another photo product.

ios.import.source.title.context: Navigation title of the first import step, which chooses where photos come from.

ios.import.source.watched_folder.detail.message: Asks for a folder and keeps importing from it as new photos appear.
ios.import.source.watched_folder.detail.context: Detail line under the watched-folder source row.

ios.import.source.watched_folder.title.context: Title of the source row that keeps importing from a folder as files appear in it. Mac only.

ios.import.state.error.title.context: Title of the failure state on import screens. The specific reason is shown underneath, from the error's own message.

ios.import.state.loading.context: Label on the spinner shown while an import screen is loading.

ios.import.state.offline.description.message: Capsule can't reach your server. Scanning still works — planning an import needs the connection back.
ios.import.state.offline.description.context: Description of the offline state on import screens.

ios.import.state.offline.title.context: Title of the offline state on import screens. Deliberately separate from an error: a scan still works offline, only checking against the server does not.

ios.import.state.retry.context: Button that repeats the failed read on an import screen.

ios.moderation.action.legal_hold.context: Moderation action: your server must not serve an item until a legal obligation ends. Your own copies are untouched.

ios.moderation.action.reinstatement.context: Moderation action: an earlier restriction has been lifted.

ios.moderation.action.suspension.context: Moderation action: your account has been suspended on this server.

ios.moderation.action.takedown.context: Moderation action: your server no longer hands out one item. The item itself is not deleted.

ios.moderation.appeal.declined.context: State of an appeal: the restriction stands.

ios.moderation.appeal.granted.context: State of an appeal: the restriction has been lifted.

ios.moderation.appeal.submitted.context: State of an appeal: filed and waiting.

ios.moderation.appeal.under_review.context: State of an appeal: being looked at.

ios.moderation.audit.appeal.context: Button that files an appeal against a moderation action.

ios.moderation.audit.none.message: Your server hasn't acted on your account.
ios.moderation.audit.none.context: Shown in place of the moderation actions list when it's empty.

ios.moderation.audit.reason_withheld.context: Shown in place of a reason when policy doesn't allow one. Stated plainly, so an empty row doesn't read as a bug.

ios.moderation.audit.when.context: Row label for when a moderation action was taken. The value is a date and time.

ios.moderation.block.since.context: Row label for when someone was blocked. The value is a date.

ios.moderation.blocks.none.context: Shown in place of the blocked list when it's empty.

ios.moderation.empty.description.message: You haven't blocked anyone or filed a report, and your server hasn't acted on your account.
ios.moderation.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the blocking and reports screen.

ios.moderation.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the blocking and reports screen.

ios.moderation.note.appeal_master_key.message: An appeal is confirmed with your account key, not your session — so you can appeal even when it's your account that's suspended.
ios.moderation.note.appeal_master_key.context: Statement about how appeals are authenticated.

ios.moderation.note.no_scanning.message: Your server can't look at your photos. They're sealed before they leave your device, so there's nothing to scan.
ios.moderation.note.no_scanning.context: Statement about what moderation cannot do. Structural, not a policy choice — do not soften it into 'we don't scan'.

ios.moderation.note.no_silent_ops.message: Every action taken on your account is recorded here. Nothing happens quietly.
ios.moderation.note.no_silent_ops.context: Statement about what moderation cannot do.

ios.moderation.reason.other.context: Reason a report was filed, including a reason this version of Capsule doesn't recognize.

ios.moderation.report.state.submitted.context: Badge on a report that has been submitted.

ios.moderation.report.submitted.context: Row label for when a report was submitted. The value is a date.

ios.moderation.reports.none.context: Shown in place of the reports list when it's empty.

ios.moderation.section.audit.context: Section header over moderation actions your server has taken, which are always recorded rather than applied silently.

ios.moderation.section.audit_footer.message: Every action your server takes is recorded here. None of them delete your photos — they stop your server serving them, and your own copies and backups are untouched.
ios.moderation.section.audit_footer.context: Section footer under the moderation actions list. Load-bearing: a takedown is a serving restriction, not destruction.

ios.moderation.section.blocks.context: Section header over the people you've blocked.

ios.moderation.section.blocks_footer.message: A blocked person is removed from albums you share with them and can't share new ones with you. What they already downloaded stays with them — nothing can reach back and take it.
ios.moderation.section.blocks_footer.context: Section footer under the blocked list. States the honest limit of a block rather than implying it undoes the past.

ios.moderation.section.how.context: Section header over the plain statement of what moderation can and can't do here.

ios.moderation.section.reports.context: Section header over reports the user has submitted.

ios.moderation.section.reports_footer.message: Reports go to whoever runs the server the content is on. Your report names the item, never its contents — nobody gains the ability to read anything by receiving it.
ios.moderation.section.reports_footer.context: Section footer under the filed reports.

ios.moderation.section.untrusted.message: Content from Servers You Haven't Trusted
ios.moderation.section.untrusted.context: Section header over content held back because it came from an unfamiliar server.

ios.moderation.section.untrusted_footer.message: Capsule holds content from servers you haven't trusted until you say so. Nothing is deleted while it waits.
ios.moderation.section.untrusted_footer.context: Section footer under the untrusted-servers list.

ios.moderation.title.context: Navigation title of the screen for blocked people, reports you've filed, and actions your server has taken.

ios.moderation.unblock.confirm.context: Confirm button in the unblock dialog. Not destructive — it lifts a restriction.

ios.moderation.unblock.confirm_message.message: They'll be able to share albums with you again. They aren't added back to anything they were removed from.

ios.moderation.unblock.confirm_title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that a block will be lifted.

ios.moderation.untrusted.consent.context: Switch that lets content from a particular server through.

ios.moderation.untrusted.withheld.context: Row label for how many items from a server are being held. The value is a number.

ios.passkey.done.authenticator.context: Row label for where the passkey is stored, such as a keychain or a security key. The value is the authenticator's own name.

ios.passkey.done.created.context: Row label for when the passkey was registered. The value is a date.

ios.passkey.done.description.message: You can now sign in with this passkey instead of your password.
ios.passkey.done.description.context: Description of the passkey success state.

ios.passkey.done.title.context: Heading of the success state after a passkey is registered.

ios.passkey.enroll.context: Primary button that starts the system passkey sheet and registers the passkey.

ios.passkey.enrolling.context: Spinner label while the passkey is being registered.

ios.passkey.loading.context: Spinner label while the passkey screen loads.

ios.passkey.name.footer.message: Something you'll recognize later, like the name of this device.
ios.passkey.name.footer.context: Footnote under the passkey name field.

ios.passkey.name.label.context: Field label for the name that will identify this passkey in the account's list.

ios.passkey.scope_note.message: A passkey replaces your password when you sign in. It can't recover your account — only your recovery phrase can do that.
ios.passkey.scope_note.context: Footnote on the passkey screen. Load-bearing: a user who mistakes a passkey for a backup would think a lost phone is survivable when it is not.

ios.passkey.subtitle.message: Sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode instead of a password.

ios.passkey.title.context: Heading of the screen that enrolls a passkey for signing in.

ios.passkey.unavailable.description.message: This device has nowhere to keep a passkey. Sign in with your password instead.
ios.passkey.unavailable.description.context: Empty-state description when passkeys are unavailable on this device.

ios.passkey.unavailable.title.message: No Place to Keep a Passkey
ios.passkey.unavailable.title.context: Empty-state title on a device with no authenticator to hold a passkey. Says what is true instead of offering a button that would fail.

ios.peering.enable.context: Switch that turns on direct syncing over the local network.

ios.peering.enable.footer.message: Your devices swap photos directly over the local network, without going through your server. Useful when the server is far away or offline.
ios.peering.enable.footer.context: Section footer under the nearby-devices switch.

ios.peering.idle.description.message: Capsule is listening. Your other devices will show up when they're on the same network.
ios.peering.idle.description.context: Description shown when nearby syncing is on and idle. Reassuring, not diagnostic.

ios.peering.idle.title.context: Title shown when nearby syncing is on but no other device has been found.

ios.peering.note.lan_only.message: Only over the local network. Nothing is exchanged across the internet this way.
ios.peering.note.lan_only.context: Statement about the scope of nearby syncing.

ios.peering.note.no_scope_knob.message: Nearby syncing follows the same What to Sync setting as everything else — there's no separate one to set.
ios.peering.note.no_scope_knob.context: Statement that nearby syncing has no settings of its own, so nobody goes looking for them.

ios.peering.note.pull_only.message: Each device asks for what it's missing. Nothing is pushed at you.
ios.peering.note.pull_only.context: Statement about how nearby syncing works.

ios.peering.note.same_account.message: Only devices signed in to your account. Someone else's device on the same network can't take part.
ios.peering.note.same_account.context: Statement about who can take part in nearby syncing.

ios.peering.peer.last_seen.context: Row label for when a nearby device was last visible. The value is a relative time.

ios.peering.section.how.context: Section header over the plain statement of what nearby syncing does.

ios.peering.section.paired.context: Section header over nearby devices already paired with this one.

ios.peering.section.transfers.context: Section header over transfers happening directly between nearby devices.

ios.peering.section.unpaired.context: Section header over nearby devices that haven't been paired.

ios.peering.section.unpaired_footer.message: Capsule only exchanges photos with devices signed in to your own account.
ios.peering.section.unpaired_footer.context: Section footer under the unpaired nearby devices.

ios.peering.title.context: Navigation title of the screen for syncing directly with your other devices over the local network.

ios.peering.transfer.receiving.context: Direction of a nearby transfer: coming to this device.

ios.peering.transfer.sending.context: Direction of a nearby transfer: leaving this device.

ios.peering.transfers.none.context: Shown in place of the nearby transfer list when it's empty.

ios.peering.trust.discovered.context: Status of a nearby device Capsule can see but hasn't paired with.

ios.peering.trust.paired.context: Status of a nearby device that has been paired with this one.

ios.peering.trust.revoked.context: Status of a nearby device whose pairing has been withdrawn.

ios.quarantine.action.discard.context: Choice for a held item: destroy what was kept. Irreversible, and always confirmed.

ios.quarantine.action.discard.descriptio.message: Destroy what was kept. This can't be undone.

ios.quarantine.action.inspect.context: Choice for a held item: look at what was kept before deciding.

ios.quarantine.action.inspect.descriptio.message: Look at what was kept, without changing anything.

ios.quarantine.action.inspect.unavailabl.message: Nothing was kept to inspect — only a record that this happened.
ios.quarantine.action.inspect.unavailabl.context: Shown when inspecting isn't possible. The option stays visible so the reason can be read.

ios.quarantine.action.repair.context: Choice for a held item: try to put it right and return it to the library.

ios.quarantine.action.repair.description.message: Try to put this right and return it to your library.

ios.quarantine.action.repair.unavailable.message: There's nothing here that repairing could fix.
ios.quarantine.action.repair.unavailable.context: Shown when repairing isn't possible. The option stays visible so the reason can be read.

ios.quarantine.detail.actions.context: Section header over the three explicit choices for a held item.

ios.quarantine.detail.actions.footer.message: There's no default here. Capsule won't choose for you, however long this waits.
ios.quarantine.detail.actions.footer.context: Footer under the choices. Nothing is pre-selected and nothing happens automatically.

ios.quarantine.detail.detected_at.context: Row label for when Capsule noticed this. The value is a date and time.

ios.quarantine.detail.preserved_bytes.context: Row label for how much of the original is being held. The value is a formatted size.

ios.quarantine.detail.reason_code.context: Row label for the stable code identifying why this item is held. The value is a short identifier, useful in a bug report, and is never translated.

ios.quarantine.detail.title.context: Navigation title of the screen for deciding what to do with one held item.

ios.quarantine.detail.what_happened.context: Section header over the explanation of why an item is being held.

ios.quarantine.detail.what_is_kept.context: Section header over where the held item's data lives and whether it can be recovered.

ios.quarantine.detail.what_is_kept.foote.message: Nothing here has been deleted or applied. It's waiting for you to decide.
ios.quarantine.detail.what_is_kept.foote.context: Footer under the what's-being-kept section. The core promise of this screen — never soften it into 'we'll clean this up'.

ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.action.context: Destructive confirm button in the discard dialog.

ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.message.message: What was kept will be destroyed for good. The record that this happened stays in your history.
ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.message.context: Message in the discard confirmation dialog.

ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.title.context: Title of the dialog confirming that held data will be destroyed.

ios.quarantine.empty.description.message: Anything Capsule holds back for you to look at will appear here.
ios.quarantine.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the needs-review list.

ios.quarantine.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when nothing is being held for review.

ios.quarantine.inspect.footer.message: The start of the kept data, shown as-is. Useful in a bug report; nothing here changes the item.
ios.quarantine.inspect.footer.context: Footer under the raw sample of a held item.

ios.quarantine.inspect.sample_size.context: Row label for how much of the held data is shown. The value is a formatted size.

ios.quarantine.inspect.title.context: Section header over the raw sample of a held item.

ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_review.message: This is waiting for you to accept it.
ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_review.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_upgrade.message: This is waiting for its album to be upgraded.
ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_upgrade.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.reason.malformed.message: The data couldn't be read as anything Capsule understands.
ios.quarantine.reason.malformed.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.reason.schema_ahead.message: This was written by a newer version of Capsule. It's kept exactly as it is, and this version won't change it.
ios.quarantine.reason.schema_ahead.context: Reason a specific item is held. Informational — the data is intact and preserved verbatim. Never word it as damaged, corrupt, or unsupported.

ios.quarantine.reason.server_rejected.message: Your server refused this. The reason code is above.
ios.quarantine.reason.server_rejected.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.reason.stale_chain.message: This is older than the version already in your library.
ios.quarantine.reason.stale_chain.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.reason.verify_rejected.message: The signature or history on this change didn't check out.
ios.quarantine.reason.verify_rejected.context: Reason a specific item is held.

ios.quarantine.row.preserved.context: Marker on a held item whose original bytes are still on this device, so it can be inspected or repaired.

ios.quarantine.storage.audit_log.context: Where a held item lives: the audit trail, which records that it happened.

ios.quarantine.storage.directory.context: Where a held item lives: a holding area on this device, with the original bytes intact.

ios.quarantine.storage.hash_table.context: Where a held item lives: a list of things Capsule declined to accept.

ios.quarantine.storage.preserved.message: The original data was kept, so you can still get this back.
ios.quarantine.storage.preserved.context: Shown when a held item's original bytes are recoverable.

ios.quarantine.storage.recorded_only.message: Only a record of what happened was kept — there's no data here to recover.
ios.quarantine.storage.recorded_only.context: Shown when a held item is a record rather than recoverable data. Say it plainly so nobody expects to get bytes back.

ios.quarantine.storage.server_inbox.context: Where a held item lives: your server is holding it until you accept it.

ios.quarantine.storage.upgrade_queue.context: Where a held item lives: a queue of writes waiting for their album to be upgraded.

ios.quarantine.surface.album_upgrade.context: Kind of held item: a change that can't be applied until its album is upgraded.

ios.quarantine.surface.album_upgrade.des.message: This change is waiting for its album to be upgraded. It'll be applied once that's done.
ios.quarantine.surface.album_upgrade.des.context: Explanation of the waiting-for-an-album-upgrade kind. Nothing is wrong — it is queued.

ios.quarantine.surface.federation.context: Kind of held item: content from a federated peer that failed verification.

ios.quarantine.surface.federation.descri.message: Content arrived from another server that Capsule couldn't verify, so it wasn't added.

ios.quarantine.surface.orphan.context: Kind of held item: a photo file found with no accompanying record.

ios.quarantine.surface.orphan.descriptio.message: A photo file was found with no record of what it is. The file is kept exactly as it was.

ios.quarantine.surface.pending_drop.context: Kind of held item: a guest uploaded something through one of your links and it's waiting for you to accept it.

ios.quarantine.surface.pending_drop.desc.message: Someone uploaded this through one of your links. It's waiting for you to accept it into your library.
ios.quarantine.surface.pending_drop.desc.context: Explanation of the awaiting-your-review kind. Perfectly normal, not a problem.

ios.quarantine.surface.restore_conflict.context: Kind of held item: a restored backup disagrees with what your library already has.

ios.quarantine.surface.restore_conflict..message: A backup you restored disagrees with what your library already has. Capsule held it rather than overwriting newer work.

ios.quarantine.surface.sidecar.context: Kind of held item: a photo's record could not be parsed.

ios.quarantine.surface.sidecar.descripti.message: A photo's record couldn't be read. The unreadable data is kept exactly as it was, in case it can be recovered.

ios.quarantine.surface.stale_revival.context: Kind of held item: something proposed a version of a photo older than the one you already have.

ios.quarantine.surface.stale_revival.des.message: Something offered an older version of a photo than the one you already have. Capsule held it rather than winding your library back.

ios.quarantine.surface.unknown.context: Kind of held item written by a newer version of Capsule that this one doesn't recognize.

ios.quarantine.surface.unknown.descripti.message: A newer version of Capsule held this back for a reason this version doesn't recognize. It's kept exactly as it is.
ios.quarantine.surface.unknown.descripti.context: Explanation of the unrecognized kind. The data is intact — never word it as damaged.

ios.quarantine.surface.verify_reject.context: Kind of held item: a change whose signature or history didn't verify, so Capsule refused to apply it.

ios.quarantine.surface.verify_reject.des.message: A change arrived that Capsule couldn't confirm came from a device on your account, so it wasn't applied.
ios.quarantine.surface.verify_reject.des.context: Explanation of the signature-didn't-check-out kind. Plain language, no blame.

ios.quarantine.title.context: Navigation title of the list of items held for a decision. Held, not broken and not deleted.

ios.quota.categories.estimated.context: Note under the usage breakdown when the server reported approximate numbers.

ios.quota.category.derivatives.context: Usage category: thumbnails and preview-sized copies.

ios.quota.category.metadata.context: Usage category: each photo's record and its placeholder image.

ios.quota.category.other.context: Usage category for anything not covered by the named ones.

ios.quota.category.trash.context: Usage category: photos deleted but not yet purged.

ios.quota.category.trash.note.message: Deleted photos still count until they're purged for good.
ios.quota.category.trash.note.context: Note under the Recently Deleted usage category, explaining why deleting alone doesn't free space yet.

ios.quota.empty.description.message: Your server hasn't reported a storage figure yet.
ios.quota.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the server storage screen.

ios.quota.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the server storage screen.

ios.quota.grace.deadline.context: Label before when edits will be paused if storage stays full. The value that follows is a relative time such as 'in 6 days'.

ios.quota.limit.unlimited.context: Shown instead of the limit figures when the server sets no storage limit, which is common for a server you run yourself.

ios.quota.link.local_storage.context: Row that opens the screen about storage used on this device, which is a different thing from server storage.

ios.quota.link.local_storage.footer.message: Freeing space on this device doesn't change what's stored on your server.
ios.quota.link.local_storage.footer.context: Footer under the link to on-device storage, drawing the distinction between the two.

ios.quota.offline.notice.message: Offline — this is the last figure your server sent
ios.quota.offline.notice.context: Notice shown when the storage figures could not be refreshed. Says plainly that the numbers may be out of date rather than presenting them as live.

ios.quota.permission.deletes.context: Row in the storage banner saying whether deleting and restoring still work. They always do — a user has to be able to delete their way back under the limit.

ios.quota.permission.metadata.context: Row in the storage banner saying whether edits that add data are still allowed.

ios.quota.permission.uploads.context: Row in the storage banner saying whether new uploads are still allowed. A checkmark or a slash beside it carries the answer.

ios.quota.remediation.contact_admin.context: Button offered when only whoever runs the server can lift the limit.

ios.quota.remediation.empty_trash.context: Button that purges deleted photos for good, which frees their space immediately.

ios.quota.remediation.review_largest.context: Button that opens the largest items so the user can decide what to remove.

ios.quota.state.grace_expired.context: Storage state: usage has stayed at the limit past the grace period, so edits are refused too.

ios.quota.state.grace_expired.descriptio.message: Storage has been full long enough that edits — captions, tags, new links — are paused as well. Reading, deleting, and restoring still work, and freeing space lifts this.
ios.quota.state.grace_expired.descriptio.context: Explanation of the edits-paused storage state. It is remediable, and the remedy is on screen.

ios.quota.state.hard_exceeded.context: Storage state: usage has reached the limit.

ios.quota.state.hard_exceeded.descriptio.message: New uploads are refused until you free space. Everything already stored is untouched and still readable.
ios.quota.state.hard_exceeded.descriptio.context: Explanation of the storage-full state. Say plainly that nothing is lost.

ios.quota.state.ok.context: Storage state: usage is below the warning level.

ios.quota.state.ok.description.context: Explanation of the plenty-of-room storage state.

ios.quota.state.soft_warning.context: Storage state: usage has passed the warning level but not the limit.

ios.quota.state.soft_warning.description.message: Uploads still work. Freeing some space now avoids being stopped later.
ios.quota.state.soft_warning.description.context: Explanation of the getting-full storage state.

ios.quota.state.suspended.context: Storage state: whoever runs the server has suspended this account.

ios.quota.state.suspended.description.message: Whoever runs this server has suspended the account. They can tell you why and what happens next.

ios.quota.state.unknown.context: Storage state written by a newer version of Capsule that this one doesn't recognize.

ios.quota.state.unknown.description.message: Your server reported a state this version of Capsule doesn't recognize.
ios.quota.state.unknown.description.context: Explanation shown for an unrecognized storage state. Not an error — a newer server may have sent it.

ios.quota.title.context: Navigation title of the screen showing how much of your server allowance is in use.

ios.quota.usage.hard_limit.context: Row label for the storage limit itself. The value is a formatted size.

ios.quota.usage.remaining.context: Row label for how much storage is left. The value is a formatted size.

ios.quota.usage.soft_limit.context: Row label for the level at which Capsule starts warning about storage. The value is a formatted size.

ios.quota.usage.title.context: Section header over the storage usage figures.

ios.quota.usage.used.context: Row label for how much server storage is in use. The value is a formatted size.

ios.recovery.passphrase.continue.context: Primary button that moves from reading the phrase to typing part of it back.

ios.recovery.passphrase.copied.context: Label the copy button changes to once the phrase has been copied.

ios.recovery.passphrase.copy.context: Button that copies the recovery phrase to the clipboard.

ios.recovery.passphrase.copy_note.message: The clipboard is cleared as soon as this device allows. Paste it straight into your password manager.

ios.recovery.passphrase.done.action.context: Primary button that leaves the finished recovery-phrase screen.

ios.recovery.passphrase.done.description.message: Keep your phrase somewhere safe. You'll need it if you ever lose every device.
ios.recovery.passphrase.done.description.context: Description of the recovery-set-up success state.

ios.recovery.passphrase.done.title.context: Heading of the success state after the type-back check passes.

ios.recovery.passphrase.empty.descriptio.message: There's no recovery phrase for this account yet.
ios.recovery.passphrase.empty.descriptio.context: Empty-state description on the recovery-phrase screen.

ios.recovery.passphrase.empty.title.context: Empty-state title when no recovery phrase is available to show.

ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.below_fl.context: Status chip when the generated phrase falls short of the required strength.

ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.defect.message: Capsule generated this phrase, so this is a fault in this version of the app and not something you did. Don't rely on this phrase — report the problem and set up recovery again.
ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.defect.context: Footnote under the strength meter when the generated phrase falls short. The user chose nothing here; the app's own generator did. Never word this as advice to pick a stronger phrase.

ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.footnote.message: Measured in bits against the minimum Capsule requires. Anything that stores your phrase can be attacked offline, so the phrase itself has to carry the strength.
ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.footnote.context: Footnote under the strength meter when the phrase clears the floor.

ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.label.context: Label above the strength meter. The value beside it reads as 'bits / required bits' and is shown as digits, not as words.

ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.meets_fl.context: Status chip when the generated phrase clears the required strength. This is a threshold, not a rating — there is no 'stronger than needed'.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.finish.context: Primary button that completes the type-back check. Enabled only when every word matches.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.no_skip.message: This step can't be skipped. A phrase nobody wrote down protects nothing.
ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.no_skip.context: Footnote under the type-back step explaining why there is no 'later' option.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.remaining.context: Label before the count of type-back words still to get right. The count is shown as digits beside it.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.show_again.context: Button that returns to the words. Available only before the check passes — the phrase is already on this screen in this session, so hiding it would only make the user guess.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.subtitle.message: Enter the words below to confirm you have the phrase.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.title.context: Heading of the step that checks a few words of the phrase were recorded.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.unverified.context: Status chip under a type-back field whose word does not match.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.verified.context: Status chip under a type-back field whose word matches.

ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.word_label.context: Label and placeholder for one type-back field. The word's position is shown as digits beside it, so this string carries no number itself.

ios.recovery.passphrase.grid.header.context: VoiceOver label for the numbered grid holding the recovery-phrase words.

ios.recovery.passphrase.loading.context: Spinner label while the recovery phrase is being prepared.

ios.recovery.passphrase.shown_once.message: This phrase is shown once. Write it down or save it somewhere safe now — nobody, including Capsule, can show it to you again.
ios.recovery.passphrase.shown_once.context: Warning placed above the words themselves, because a user who has already read the phrase will not scroll back for a caveat.

ios.recovery.passphrase.subtitle.message: This phrase is the only way back into your library if you lose your devices. Write it down before you continue.
ios.recovery.passphrase.subtitle.context: Subtitle of the recovery-phrase screen. There is no way to skip this step.

ios.recovery.passphrase.title.context: Heading of the screen that shows the recovery phrase once and then asks for part of it back.

ios.recovery.passphrase.word_position.context: VoiceOver label for one word in the recovery-phrase grid. The spoken value is the word's position followed by the word itself.

ios.recovery.verify.badge.description.message: Capsule will keep showing this until you check. It still won't stop you doing anything.
ios.recovery.verify.badge.description.context: Footnote under the outstanding-check chip. Visibility escalates; consequence never does.

ios.recovery.verify.badge.persistent.context: Status chip once the check has been put off as often as Capsule allows.

ios.recovery.verify.cadence.context: Label before the current interval between checks. The number of days follows as digits.

ios.recovery.verify.checking.context: Spinner label while the typed phrase is being checked.

ios.recovery.verify.due.context: Status chip when a recovery check is due.

ios.recovery.verify.field.footer.message: Typed here only to check it. It isn't sent anywhere and isn't stored.
ios.recovery.verify.field.footer.context: Footnote under the recovery-phrase field on the check screen.

ios.recovery.verify.field.label.context: Field label where the recovery phrase is typed for the check.

ios.recovery.verify.loading.context: Spinner label while the recovery check loads its schedule.

ios.recovery.verify.lost.context: Button for someone who no longer has their recovery phrase, which leads to setting up a new one.

ios.recovery.verify.never_blocks.message: This check never blocks anything. Your library keeps working either way.
ios.recovery.verify.never_blocks.context: Footnote at the foot of the recovery check.

ios.recovery.verify.not_armed.descriptio.message: This account recovers through whoever sponsors it, so it has no phrase of its own.
ios.recovery.verify.not_armed.descriptio.context: Empty-state description for a sponsored account. Not an error, and not something the user can change here.

ios.recovery.verify.not_armed.title.context: Empty-state title for an account whose recovery runs through a sponsor rather than its own phrase.

ios.recovery.verify.outcome.inconclusive.context: Status chip when the check could not run — the stored key was unreachable. Explicitly not a failed check, and nothing is recorded against the user.

ios.recovery.verify.outcome.mismatch.context: Status chip when the typed phrase did not open the account's stored key.

ios.recovery.verify.outcome.verified.context: Status chip when the typed phrase opened the account's stored key.

ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.action.context: Primary button that starts the new-recovery-phrase flow.

ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.description.message: Capsule can give you a new phrase for the same account key. Your photos aren't touched and nothing is re-encrypted.
ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.description.context: Description of the new-phrase offer. Important: this replaces the phrase, not the key, so no data changes.

ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.title.context: Heading of the offer that appears after several unsuccessful checks.

ios.recovery.verify.snooze.one_day.context: Button that puts the recovery check off by one day.

ios.recovery.verify.snooze.one_week.context: Button that puts the recovery check off by a week.

ios.recovery.verify.submit.context: Primary button that runs the recovery check.

ios.recovery.verify.subtitle.message: A quick check that the phrase you saved still works. Nothing depends on doing it now.
ios.recovery.verify.subtitle.context: Subtitle of the recovery check. This prompt never blocks anything — the copy must not imply it does.

ios.recovery.verify.title.context: Heading of the periodic prompt asking whether the recovery phrase is still at hand.

ios.recovery.verify.unconfigured.descrip.message: There's no recovery phrase on this account yet, so there's nothing to check.
ios.recovery.verify.unconfigured.descrip.context: Empty-state description when recovery is not configured.

ios.recovery.verify.unconfigured.title.context: Empty-state title when this account has no recovery phrase to check.

ios.restore.commit.confirm.action.context: Destructive confirm button in the restore confirmation sheet.

ios.restore.commit.confirm.field.context: Field label where the confirmation phrase is typed. The phrase itself is shown above and is never translated.

ios.restore.commit.confirm.message.message: This writes the changes you just reviewed into your library. Type the phrase below to confirm.
ios.restore.commit.confirm.message.context: Message in the restore confirmation sheet.

ios.restore.commit.confirm.title.context: Heading of the typed-phrase confirmation sheet for applying a restore.

ios.restore.commit.description.message: Applies everything listed above to your library.
ios.restore.commit.description.context: Description of the commit restore step.

ios.restore.commit.done.context: Status chip once the restore has been applied.

ios.restore.commit.note.message: Available only after a comparison that passed its checks. You'll be asked to type a phrase to confirm.

ios.restore.commit.open.context: Destructive button that opens the typed confirmation. The ellipsis marks that a confirmation follows.

ios.restore.commit.title.context: Heading of the final restore step, which actually writes the changes.

ios.restore.diff.added.context: Row label for how many items the restore would bring back. The count is shown as digits.

ios.restore.diff.already_present.context: Row label for how many items in the backup are already in the library. The count is shown as digits.

ios.restore.diff.conflicting.context: Row label for how many items differ between the backup and the library. The count is shown as digits. These are held for you to resolve, never applied automatically.

ios.restore.diff.reconciliation_note.message: Anything that differs is held for you to decide, never applied on its own. An old backup won't bring back a photo you deleted since.

ios.restore.diff.superseded.context: Row label for how many items your library has a newer version of than the backup. The count is shown as digits.

ios.restore.dry_run.description.message: Compares the backup with your library and reports what restoring it would do. Still nothing is changed.
ios.restore.dry_run.description.context: Description of the dry-run restore step.

ios.restore.dry_run.run.context: Button that runs the dry-run comparison.

ios.restore.dry_run.title.context: Heading of the second restore step, which compares the backup against what is already here.

ios.restore.preview.artifact_version.context: Row label for the backup file's format version. The value is a number.

ios.restore.preview.assets.context: Row label for how many items the backup contains. The count is shown as digits beside it.

ios.restore.preview.description.message: Reads the backup and reports what it holds. Nothing is changed.
ios.restore.preview.description.context: Description of the preview restore step.

ios.restore.preview.exported.context: Row label for when the backup was made. The value is a date.

ios.restore.preview.exporter.context: Row label for the device that made the backup. The value is a device model name.

ios.restore.preview.run.context: Button that reads the backup and shows its contents.

ios.restore.preview.size.context: Row label for the total size of the backup. The value is a formatted file size.

ios.restore.preview.title.context: Heading of the first restore step, which reads the backup's contents without touching anything.

ios.restore.shamir.description.message: Your recovery secret can be split into shares held by different people or places. Enough of them together rebuild it; one on its own reveals nothing.
ios.restore.shamir.description.context: Description of the split-share restore section. The rebuilding happens entirely on this device.

ios.restore.shamir.empty.message: No shares are available on this device.
ios.restore.shamir.empty.context: Shown in place of the share list when there are none.

ios.restore.shamir.invalidated.context: Status chip on a share that a later rotation killed. Dead shares stay listed on purpose — better to learn now than on the day it's needed.

ios.restore.shamir.invalidated_note.message: This share was replaced and no longer counts. Ask whoever holds it to destroy it, and give them the current one.

ios.restore.shamir.issued.context: Row label for when a share was created. The value is a date.

ios.restore.shamir.reconstruct.context: Primary button that rebuilds the recovery secret from the selected shares. Enabled only once enough valid shares are selected.

ios.restore.shamir.reconstructing.context: Spinner label while the recovery secret is being rebuilt from shares.

ios.restore.shamir.restored.context: Row label for the account the rebuilt shares belong to. The value is the account handle.

ios.restore.shamir.threshold.context: Label before the number of shares required to rebuild the secret. The number is shown as digits beside it.

ios.restore.shamir.title.context: Heading of the section that rebuilds the account key from split recovery shares.

ios.restore.subtitle.message: Look at what's in this backup and see what it would change before anything is applied.
ios.restore.subtitle.context: Subtitle of the restore screen. A dry run always comes first; committing is never the default.

ios.restore.title.context: Heading of the screen that restores a backup file: preview, then a dry run, then a typed confirmation.

ios.restore.verify.ledger_complete.context: Status chip when the backup carries the keys for everything inside it.

ios.restore.verify.ledger_incomplete.context: Status chip when the backup is missing keys for some of its contents, which means those photos are unrecoverable from it. This blocks restoring — it is a refusal, not a warning.

ios.restore.verify.refused.message: Capsule won't restore this backup while the checks above are failing. The file is left exactly as it is.
ios.restore.verify.refused.context: Explanation shown when a check has taken restoring off the table, so the disabled button is never a silent refusal.

ios.restore.verify.signatures_broken.context: Status chip when the backup's signatures do not verify, so nothing it claims about its contents can be trusted. This blocks restoring — it is a refusal, not a warning.

ios.restore.verify.signatures_intact.context: Status chip when the backup's signatures verify, so its list of contents can be trusted.

ios.restore.working.context: Spinner label while a restore step is running.

ios.settings.account.actions.footer.message: Signing out leaves your photos on this device alone. Nothing is deleted.
ios.settings.account.actions.footer.context: Section footer under the account actions.

ios.settings.account.actions.header.context: Section header over signing out and related actions.

ios.settings.account.confirm_local_auth.context: Button that satisfies the device unlock the session is waiting on.

ios.settings.account.display_name.context: Row label for the name other people see.

ios.settings.account.empty.description.message: Connect a server to use Capsule with an account.
ios.settings.account.empty.description.context: Empty-state description on the Account screen.

ios.settings.account.empty.title.context: Empty-state title on the Account screen.

ios.settings.account.handle.context: Row label for the account handle, which has the form user@yourserver.tld.

ios.settings.account.home_server.context: Row label for the server this account lives on.

ios.settings.account.identity.footer.message: Your handle is bound to this server. Your identity isn't — you keep it if you move.
ios.settings.account.identity.footer.context: Section footer under the account identity rows.

ios.settings.account.identity.header.context: Section header over the account's handle, name, and server.

ios.settings.account.portability.body.message: You can move to a different server and keep your identity, your photos, and everyone you share with.
ios.settings.account.portability.body.context: Note on the Account screen about being able to leave.

ios.settings.account.revoke_all.context: Destructive button that ends every session on the account.

ios.settings.account.revoke_all.confirm..context: Destructive confirm button in the sign-out-everywhere dialog.

ios.settings.account.revoke_all.confirm..message: Every device, including this one, will be signed out. You'll be asked to confirm with your account key. Your photos stay where they are.
ios.settings.account.revoke_all.confirm..context: Message in the sign-out-everywhere dialog. The proof requirement is stated in advance rather than discovered when the request fails.
Title of the dialog confirming that every session will end.

ios.settings.account.sessions.current.context: Status marking the session you're using right now.

ios.settings.account.sessions.expires.context: Row label for when a session stops working. The value is a date.

ios.settings.account.sessions.footer.message: Ending one session signs out that device only. Everything else keeps working.
ios.settings.account.sessions.footer.context: Section footer under the sessions list.

ios.settings.account.sessions.header.context: Section header over the sign-ins currently active on this account.

ios.settings.account.sessions.last_used.context: Row label for when a session was last active. The value is a date and time.

ios.settings.account.sessions.none.context: Shown when this account has no other live sessions.

ios.settings.account.sessions.other.context: Status marking a session on some other device.

ios.settings.account.sessions.revoke.context: Destructive button that ends one other session.

ios.settings.account.sessions.session.context: Row label for one sign-in. The status beside it says whether it's the current one.

ios.settings.account.signout.context: Destructive button that signs this device out.

ios.settings.account.signout.confirm.act.context: Destructive confirm button in the sign-out dialog.

ios.settings.account.signout.confirm.mes.message: This device signs out of your server. Photos already on it stay where they are.

ios.settings.account.signout.confirm.tit.context: Title of the dialog confirming sign-out on this device.

ios.settings.account.state.expired.context: Session standing: the session is no longer valid.
